info.title: Xorgate Core API
info.description:
The REST API behind xorgate: organizations, workspaces, devices, device configuration,
recorded media, and stored telemetry.

**Versioning.** Every path in this document is served under `/v1`, and that prefix is part
of the path rather than of the host, so a base URL is a bare origin such as
`https://api-dev.xorgate.io` and the operations below append `/v1/...` to it. There is no
unversioned surface: a request without the prefix is a 404.

**Authentication.** Every endpoint except `/health` and this document requires
`Authorization: Bearer <credential>`, and there are three kinds, told apart by their prefix in
that one header. A Cognito **ID** token (not an access token) authenticates a person; a user
row is created on first successful verification. An **API key** from `POST /api-keys` (`xg_`)
authenticates a program and acts inside the organization it was minted from with its own
`role`; it is a server-side credential and must never reach a browser. A **session token**
from `POST /auth/session-tokens` (`xgs_`) is what a browser or a mobile app holds instead: your
server exchanges its key for one, it expires within the hour, it is never more privileged than
the key, and it can be confined to a single workspace.

Most operations take any of the three. The exceptions are narrow and deliberate: eight
operations accept only an ID token, because they describe or act on a person (the four `/me`
operations, `GET`/`POST /organizations`, and the two live-access operations), and
`POST /auth/session-tokens` accepts only an API key.

**Tenancy.** Org-scoped endpoints resolve the active organization from the `X-Organization-Id`
header, falling back to your sole membership if you have exactly one. A caller in more than one
organization who omits the header gets `400 ORGANIZATION_REQUIRED`, so clients should always
send it. An API key or session token needs no header at all: its organization is fixed by the
row behind it, and a header naming a different organization is `403 FORBIDDEN`.
`X-Workspace-Id` narrows `GET /devices` and is required by `POST /device-registrations`.

**Workspaces are a filter, with one exception.** For a person or an API key, every workspace in
the organization is visible and `X-Workspace-Id` merely narrows a list. For a session token
minted with a `workspaceId` it is an enforced BOUNDARY: device reads and writes are confined to
that workspace, a contradicting `X-Workspace-Id` is `403 WORKSPACE_MISMATCH`, and
organization-wide operations (memberships, API keys, organization settings, workspace writes)
are `403 WORKSPACE_SCOPED` whatever role the token carries. That is how a consumer running its
own multi-tenancy maps its customers onto workspaces and hands each one a credential that
cannot reach the others.

**Envelopes.** Responses are always a named object, never a bare array: `{devices, page}`,
`{device}`, `{organizations}`. Fields are camelCase; three envelope KEYS are snake_case
(`api_keys`, `api_key`/`plaintext_key`, `device_model`/`device_models`) because they mirror
their Postgres table names, and that stays as-is on the wire. DELETE returns `204` with an
empty body, device commands return `202`, and errors are uniformly
`{"error": {"code", "message", "details?"}}`.

**Pagination.** Only `GET /devices`, `GET /devices/{id}/sessions`,
`GET /devices/{id}/telemetry/readings`, `GET /devices/{id}/telemetry/sessions` and
`GET /workflow-templates`, `GET /webhooks` and `GET /webhooks/{id}/deliveries` paginate; they accept
`limit`/`offset`/`order`/`sort`
and return a `page` block. Every other list endpoint returns its whole collection unbounded:
organizations, memberships, workspaces, device models, API keys, video channels, the
workflow-template tag vocabulary, and a session
segment index `GET /devices/{id}/telemetry` is not a list endpoint either. It caps rows and
reports `truncated`.

**The live plane.** Live telemetry and live video do not flow through this API: they are
streaming protocols the client speaks directly, entered with a signed connection rather than
with a bearer token. `POST /auth/live-credentials` is what signs it, and any of the three
credentials may call it. What comes back is confined to the same tenant the calling credential
is: a credential vended for a workspace receives that workspace's devices and is refused a
sibling workspace's, on both planes and by the credential itself. Treat the response as
opaque. The two operations in the Live section are the first-party dashboard's own path and
are not part of a third-party integration.

**What is not here.** The Workflows and AI surface is deliberately undocumented while it is
still moving. The three exceptions are the workflow-template READS below, which exist because
a program discovers templates by tag and acts on them; authoring a template, publishing it,
attaching it to a device and reading its runs are all still editor-side and undocumented.

tags.name: Users
tags.description: Who the caller is, and which organizations they can act in.

tags.name: Organizations
tags.description: The billing and ownership boundary. Everything else hangs off one.

tags.name: Memberships
tags.description: Who belongs to an organization, and with what role.

tags.name: API Keys
tags.description: Organization-scoped keys. Send one as `Authorization: Bearer xg_...` to authenticate any organization-scoped operation, at the role the key was minted with.

tags.name: Auth
tags.description: Exchanging an API key for a short-lived token your client can hold. The one endpoint a third-party integration is built on.

tags.name: Workspaces
tags.description: The grouping devices belong to, one level below an organization. Also the tenancy unit for a consumer running its own multi-tenancy: a session token can be confined to one.

tags.name: Device Models
tags.description: The platform-wide hardware catalog. Reading is open to any authenticated caller; writing needs a platform admin.

tags.name: Devices
tags.description: Device records, their configuration document, their IoT identity, and the one-shot commands you can send them.

tags.name: Device Simulations
tags.description: Devices with no hardware: the real device agent replaying a recorded drive on a loop, hosted for you. Create one here; everything else about it is a normal device under /devices.

tags.name: Transfer Offers
tags.description: Handing a device to an organization you have no membership in. The source mints a code, the destination redeems it. A move between workspaces of the SAME organization needs none of this — see POST /devices/{id}/transfer.

tags.name: Device Registrations
tags.description: Onboarding a physical device with a short-lived code and the install script.

tags.name: Telemetry
tags.description: Stored sensor readings. The live 1 Hz feed does not come through this API.

tags.name: Media Sessions
tags.description: Video recorded on the device and uploaded as segments: sessions, runs, segment index, playback URLs, and replay manifests.

tags.name: Live
tags.description: Bootstrap for the live plane: video channel metadata, and the access grant the first-party dashboard needs.

tags.name: Workflow Templates
tags.description: The reusable processing graphs an organization has authored, and the tags a program finds them by. Reading only: authoring happens in the editor.

tags.name: Webhooks
tags.description: Signed HTTPS callbacks when something happens: a device goes online or offline, a recording session starts, ends or completes, a workflow emits an event. Register an endpoint once, then route to it from a device (`PUT /devices/{id}/webhooks`) or from a workflow's Emit Event node. Deliveries follow Standard Webhooks and are retried for about 44 hours. The payload of each event type is under `x-webhooks`.

tags.name: Search
tags.description: Cross-resource lookup within the active organization.

BearerAuth.description: A Cognito **ID** token (not an access token). Users are created just-in-time on first successful verification. This is what a signed-in browser session sends. A handful of operations accept ONLY this, because they describe or act on a person: the four `/me` operations, both `/organizations` collection operations, and the two live-access operations.

ApiKeyAuth.description: An API key from `POST /api-keys`, sent in the same header as a token: `Authorization: Bearer xg_...`. The server tells the two apart by the `xg_` prefix, so no extra header is involved. A key is bound to one organization by the row it was minted from, which makes `X-Organization-Id` redundant; sending a DIFFERENT organization is `403 FORBIDDEN` rather than an ignored header. The key acts with its own `role` (default `member`), so every role gate in this document applies to it unchanged. Keys carry no user, so operations that need one refuse them with `401 USER_CREDENTIAL_REQUIRED`.

SessionTokenAuth.description:
A short-lived token from `POST /auth/session-tokens`, sent in the same header as the other two: `Authorization: Bearer xgs_...`. This is the only xorgate credential a browser or a mobile binary should ever hold — your server exchanges its API key for one, per end user, per request if you like.

It carries the key's organization and the key's role (never more), expires within the hour, and dies the moment the key that minted it is deleted. It can also be confined to ONE workspace, which is the only place in this API where a workspace is a boundary rather than a filter: such a token sees that workspace's devices and nothing else, gets `403 WORKSPACE_MISMATCH` for an `X-Workspace-Id` naming another workspace, and `403 WORKSPACE_SCOPED` on organization-wide operations regardless of its role. Like a key it has no user, so person-scoped operations refuse it with `401 USER_CREDENTIAL_REQUIRED`.

OrganizationIdHeader.name: X-Organization-Id
OrganizationIdHeader.description: Active organization UUID. Resolution order: this header if present (it must match one of your memberships, else `403 FORBIDDEN`), otherwise your sole membership. A caller who belongs to more than one organization and omits it gets `400 ORGANIZATION_REQUIRED`, and a caller who belongs to none gets `403 NO_ORGANIZATION`. Practically: always send it. When the credential is an API key the organization comes from the key itself, so this header is optional and never required; sending one that is not the key's organization is `403 FORBIDDEN`, deliberately not a silent override.

WorkspaceIdHeader.name: X-Workspace-Id
WorkspaceIdHeader.description:
Optional workspace UUID. On `GET /devices` it filters the result to that workspace (a workspace outside the active organization yields an EMPTY page, not an error). Required on `POST /device-registrations`.

One credential changes what this header means. For a **workspace-scoped session token** the workspace is already fixed, so the header is redundant: sending the token's own workspace is accepted, sending a different one is `403 WORKSPACE_MISMATCH` rather than an empty result, and omitting it on `POST /device-registrations` is fine because the token supplies it.

SegmentSeqPath.name: seq
SegmentSeqPath.description: Segment sequence number within the session (0-based).

LimitQuery.name: limit
LimitQuery.description: Page size. Default 100; the endpoint maximum is 500 everywhere the shared list dialect applies. A value above the maximum, a non-integer, or a value below 1 is a 400. (Before API productization the over-maximum case was silently clamped; it now rejects, so a consumer cannot ship a page that quietly shows 500 of 4,000 rows.)

OffsetQuery.name: offset
OffsetQuery.description: Rows to skip. A non-integer is a 400; an offset past the end returns an empty page.

OrderQuery.name: order
OrderQuery.description: Sort direction of the sort column this endpoint uses.

FromQuery.name: from
FromQuery.description: Range start (inclusive), ISO-8601. Must be earlier than `to`.

WebhookEndpoint.description: A registered receiver. The signing secret is never part of it.

disabledReason.description: `manual` (PATCH), `gone` (the endpoint answered 410) or `failing` (auto-disabled after repeated exhausted deliveries).

error.description: Timeout, network error or "redirect not followed".

WebhookEventEnvelope.description: The JSON body of every delivery. Dedupe on `id` (also the `webhook-id` header): delivery is at-least-once. `createdAt` is when xorgate detected the event (server clock).

scenarioId.description: The scenario the device is on now: its `simulation` config namespace, or the one it was created with when the namespace is absent.

hostId.description: The host that last reported this simulation.

hostState.description: `pending` until a host first reports it. `running` means the agent in the container is connected, not merely that the container is up; `stopped` is a sim parked by `power_off` (see `POST /device-simulations/{id}/start`).

createdBy.description: User id or API key id.

ApiError.description: The uniform error envelope. Every non-2xx response in this API has this shape; `code` is stable and machine-readable, `message` is human-facing and may change.

code.description: Stable error code. The full set a client can see: `UNAUTHORIZED` (401), `ORGANIZATION_REQUIRED` (400, multi-org caller sent no `X-Organization-Id`), `BAD_REQUEST` (400), `FORBIDDEN` / `NO_ORGANIZATION` / `INSUFFICIENT_ROLE` (403), `NOT_FOUND` (404), `METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED` (405), `CONFLICT` / `PURGE_IN_PROGRESS` / `TRANSFER_PENDING` / `SIMULATION_QUOTA_EXCEEDED` (409), `PURGE_DISPATCH_FAILED` / `SIMULATION_PROVISION_FAILED` (502), `SERVER_ERROR` (500, an unhandled failure; quote `requestId` when reporting it), `CONFIG_PUBLISH_FAILED` / `COMMAND_PUBLISH_FAILED` / `DIST_MANIFEST_UNAVAILABLE` / `DIST_MANIFEST_INVALID` (502).

details.description: Present only on the errors that carry structured context.

requestId.description: The API Gateway request id of the failed call, the same id the access log records. Quote it in a support ticket to make the failure findable. Present on every error the API itself produced; absent only on errors generated by the gateway in front of it (throttling 429s, malformed-request 4xxs).

PageMeta.description: Pagination block returned alongside the items by every endpoint that speaks the list dialect (see the `limit`/`offset`/`order`/`sort` parameters). `limit` and `offset` echo the request, and `total` is the exact match count under the same filters, except on `GET /devices/{id}/telemetry/readings`, the one endpoint whose table is large enough that an exact count times out, which caps it and says so via `totalIsCapped`.

totalIsCapped.description: Only `GET /devices/{id}/telemetry/readings` sets this. True means more rows match than `total` reports and only the first `total` are addressable.

coveredFrom.description: Only `GET /devices/{id}/telemetry/readings`. Oldest addressable sample under this filter; absent when nothing matches.

coveredTo.description: Only `GET /devices/{id}/telemetry/readings`. Newest addressable sample under this filter; absent when nothing matches.

avatarUrl.description: Presigned GET for the profile picture, valid one hour, or null when the user has none. Minted per response — the bucket is private, so the URL is the only way to read the object and it cannot be cached past its expiry. Present on the `/me` operations only; elsewhere a user block is the row and carries no picture.

role.description: PLATFORM role, distinct from the per-organization membership role. Only `admin` may write the device-model catalog.

created_at.description: snake_case on the wire: `GET /me` serializes the users row verbatim. The SDKs normalize it to `createdAt`.

Organization.description: Organization rows serialize verbatim from Postgres, so their timestamps are snake_case while most of this API is camelCase. The SDKs normalize; the wire format stays as-is.

logoUrl.description: Presigned GET for the organization logo, valid one hour, or null when it has none. Minted per response — the bucket is private, so the URL is the only way to read the object and it cannot be cached past its expiry. Clients that draw a placeholder fall back to the initials of `name`.

ApiKey.description: API key metadata. `hashedKey` is never returned; the plaintext key is shown exactly once, at creation. A key is a real credential: send it as `Authorization: Bearer xg_...` to any organization-scoped operation, and it acts with its own `role` inside the organization it was minted from. `scope` remains recorded but unenforced.

scope.description: Validated on create, but not enforced anywhere: every key behaves as `cloud` (server-to-server) regardless of what is recorded here.

role.description: The role this key acts with, using the same vocabulary and the same gates as a membership role. The default `member` can write devices, workspaces and device registrations, and read everything, but cannot touch memberships, API keys or organization settings. A key is never a PLATFORM admin, so device-model writes are closed to every key regardless of this field.

keyPrefix.description: The first 8 characters of the plaintext, stored so you can tell which key a holder has. **Null for any key minted before this field existed** and unbackfillable, because only the SHA-256 was ever stored. Show those as unknown rather than guessing.

expiresAt.description: When the key stops authenticating. Null means never, which is what every key minted before this field existed is. After it passes, requests get `401 API_KEY_EXPIRED`.

lastUsedAt.description: Roughly when this key last authenticated a request, and null until it does. Deliberately approximate: the write is throttled to at most once per minute per serving process and is fire-and-forget, so it never delays or fails a request. Read it as a liveness hint for finding unused keys, not as an audit log.

revokedAt.description: Set means the key is dead: requests get `401 API_KEY_REVOKED`. No endpoint sets this today; `DELETE /api-keys/{id}` removes the row outright instead.

CreateSessionTokenInput.description: Every field is optional; an empty body mints an org-scoped token at the default TTL.

workspaceId.description: Confine the token to one workspace. Omit (or null) for the whole organization. A workspace outside the key's organization is `403`, and so is one that does not exist — telling those two apart would confirm other organizations' workspace ids.

ttlSeconds.description: Lifetime in seconds. Out-of-range values are REJECTED rather than clamped: a credential lifetime you believe you got and did not is a bug that surfaces as mysterious 401s later. Mint a fresh token rather than reaching for the maximum.

SessionToken.description: A minted session token. Flat rather than wrapped in a named envelope, because it is a credential rather than a resource and there is nothing to read back later.

id.description: Identifies the token in your own logs. It is NOT a credential and cannot be exchanged for one.

token.description: The credential. Returned exactly once — only its SHA-256 is stored. Send it as `Authorization: Bearer xgs_...`, the same header everything else uses.

expiresAt.description: After this, requests get `401 SESSION_TOKEN_EXPIRED`. Refresh before it, not after.

workspaceId.description: Echo of the requested scope. Null means the token sees the whole organization.

role.description: Inherited from the minting key. The role actually in force on a request is the lower of this and the key's role at that moment.

live.description: Coordinates for the live plane, which does not flow through this API. They ride along with the token so a client's configuration is just the API base URL, and so that moving them needs no consumer redeploy.

realtimeEndpoint.description: Host for the live telemetry stream (MQTT over WebSockets).

CreateLiveCredentialsInput.description: Every field is optional. An empty body vends for whatever the calling credential already reaches: one workspace if it is a workspace-scoped session token, the whole organization otherwise.

workspaceId.description: Narrow the credentials to one workspace. This is how the PROXIED shape works: your server holds one API key for your whole organization and vends per customer. It can only ever narrow — a workspace outside the calling credential's scope is `403 WORKSPACE_NOT_IN_SCOPE`.

ttlSeconds.description: Lifetime in seconds. Out-of-range values are REJECTED rather than clamped, same as for session tokens. The floor is higher than a session token's because a live connection that outlives its credentials has to be torn down and re-established.

LiveCredentials.description: Credentials for the live plane. **Opaque**: pass the object to the SDK and do not read or persist individual fields. Flat rather than wrapped, because it is a credential rather than a resource and there is nothing to read back later.

accessKeyId.description: Part of the signature. Do not interpret.

secretAccessKey.description: Part of the signature. Do not interpret, do not log, and do not store beyond the lifetime below.

sessionToken.description: Part of the signature. Do not interpret.

expiration.description: When these stop working. Mint again shortly before it; a live connection is not renewed in place, it is re-established.

organizationId.description: Echo of the scope these credentials were vended for.

workspaceId.description: Echo of the requested scope. Null means the whole organization. Worth asserting on in the proxied shape: it is the confirmation that you vended for the customer you meant to.

live.description: The same coordinates `POST /auth/session-tokens` returns, repeated here because the proxied shape never calls that endpoint and would otherwise have nowhere to learn them.

realtimeEndpoint.description: Host for the live telemetry stream (MQTT over WebSockets).

logoUrl.description: Presigned GET for the workspace logo, valid one hour, or null when it has none. Same contract as `Organization.logoUrl`.

IoCapabilities.description:
What a device model can do (`device_models.io_capabilities`). Each declared leaf maps to one telemetry metric namespace and/or one media stream key, and every section is optional so partial-capability hardware is describable. `media.video[].key` is what becomes a video channel at provisioning time; `sensors.imu` field lists become the `imu.<prefix>_<field>` metrics; `comm` and `system` field lists become the `gps`, `signal` and `system` metric namespaces; a v2 `peripherals.obd.fields` list becomes the `obd` namespace (an attached ELM327 OBD-II reader; the adapter address itself is a per-device setting, not a model fact).

IMPORTANT: this shape is NOT enforced when you write a device model. `POST`/`PUT /device-models` accept any JSON object here. It IS parsed at provisioning time, and a document that fails to parse yields NO video stream keys, so the device is provisioned with zero video channels and live video silently never works. Validate against this schema yourself before writing.

agentVersion.description: Installed xorgate-device-agent build (CI short sha on dev, release tag on prod), mirrored from the device's own config report, and read-only. null until the device reports a build.

firmwareVersion.description: DEPRECATED alias for agentVersion; removed once clients migrate.

agent.description: Which device agent the device runs. Set from its registration at claim, then promoted to `rust` (never demoted) when the device reports `effective.agent.runtime: "rust"`. Compare `agentVersion` against `GET /device-dist/latest?agent=<this>`. Read-only.

status.description: Machine-managed: telemetry ingest, the MQTT last-will and the offline sweeper own this. Writing it through `PUT /devices/{id}` is rejected 400.

simulated.description: A device-simulator device: the real agent replaying a recorded drive in a container, created by `POST /device-simulations`. Fixed at creation and never writable. Everything else about it is a normal device; only a simulated device accepts the `simulation` config namespace.

obdScanRequestedAt.description: When the last `POST /devices/{id}/commands/obd-scan` was accepted for this device; the server refuses another inside 60 s of it. null = never scanned. Machine-managed.

needsModel.description: Probe-at-claim could not pick a device model unambiguously; the device carries its registration's fallback model until an operator confirms one via `PUT /devices/{id}` `{deviceModelId}`, which clears this.

config.description: Everything this device is told, in one namespaced document. Written by PATCH /devices/{id}/config and published as a retained MQTT message. Namespaces the cloud has reverted are STRIPPED from this view, so a namespace is either configured or absent, never present-but-null.

configRev.description: Monotonic config revision, bumped on every config write and carried on the retained message as `rev`. The device applies a document newer than its last-applied rev; `configRev > reportedConfig.rev` on an online device means the change is still pending.

uiPrefs.description: Cloud-only presentation preferences. Never delivered to the device.

reportedConfig.description: Last config report from the device, mirrored off `xorgate/devices/{id}/config/reported`; null until the device has reported at least once (a pre-Phase-3 agent never does). Shape: `{ v, deviceId, ts, rev, origin, effective, status }`. `rev` is the last desired revision the device applied (0 = never received one), `origin` is `cloud`/`local`/`boot`, `effective` holds the post-clamp values actually in force (an absent namespace means device defaults, and `gnssAntBias` is the value the modem daemon applied, not the one requested), and `status` carries a per-namespace `{ state: applied|adjusted|rejected, at, detail?, reason? }`. There is no `pending` state on the wire: the reader computes it as `configRev > reportedConfig.rev` on an online device. `effective.agent.mode` is reported-only (`sim`/`real`): it is never cloud-settable and never gets a `status` entry. `effective.sim` (SIM presence, state, ICCID, phone number, carrier, registration) and `effective.uplink` (which interface carries the default route) are reported-only in exactly the same way, because a device cannot be TOLD its ICCID, so neither is a config namespace and neither ever carries a `status`. Both are ABSENT when the device has not reported them, which means unknown and never "no SIM". `effective.apn` is reported-only too: the modem daemon's APN apply machinery: `{ applied, requested?, state: in-force|applying|rolled-back|rejected, last_error?, changed_at? }`. `applied` is the APN actually in the modem's data context (the `cellular` namespace's `effective.cellular.apn` mirrors it while a change is in flight); an ABSENT `apn` block means the daemon predates the rollback machinery, and a UI must refuse to write the `cellular` namespace to such a device, since there is no safety net there. An `origin: "local"` report additionally carries `changed`, the namespaces a local writer altered on the device (`null` = reverted to device defaults); those are validated and merged into `config`, which bumps `configRev` and republishes, unless a newer cloud revision already landed, in which case the cloud value wins and the local change is discarded.

gnssAntBias.description: DEPRECATED. Read `config.gnssAntBias`. Dual-written during the transition window and dropped by a follow-up migration.

GnssAntBias.description: GPS antenna bias (`gnssAntBias`): true powers an active antenna over the coax, false (default) is the passive/bias-off hardware-safe state.

enabled.description: Apply the correction. false publishes sensor-frame euler angles as-is.

rollDeg.description: Roll rotation of the sensor relative to the vehicle, degrees.

pitchDeg.description: Pitch rotation of the sensor relative to the vehicle, degrees.

yawDeg.description: Yaw rotation of the sensor relative to the vehicle, degrees.

ImuMountConfig.description: IMU mounting correction (`imuMount` namespace): how the sensor is physically rotated relative to the vehicle (ZYX euler, degrees). All four fields are required. Applied live by the IMU collector; absent = no correction.

rateHz.description: Target sample rate. Each sensor group is additionally capped by its native cadence (IMU 20 Hz, GPS 1 Hz, system 1 Hz). Default 1.

preset.description: Closed quality preset table (bounded CPU cost). Default 720p15-1mbps.

segmentSeconds.description: Segment length — the unit of upload, retry and eviction. Default 60.

bootDefer.description: Boot power staging: auto (default) defers heavy encoders at boot only when the negotiated PSU budget is below bootDeferMinBudgetMa; always defers every boot; off starts everything immediately.

bootDeferMaxSecs.description: Hard cap on the boot defer in seconds. Default 90; 0 = feature off.

bootDeferMinBudgetMa.description: auto mode skips the defer when the negotiated supply budget (mA) is at or above this. Default 5000 (a true 5 V/5 A PD supply).

gpsGate.description: GPS/LTE video gate: hold video (recording AND live) until the modem stops converting power into value — LTE connected with a GPS fix, a declared dead zone, a sustained no-signal sky, or gpsGateMaxSecs. auto (default) applies it only below bootDeferMinBudgetMa; always gates every boot; off disables it. Telemetry recording is never gated.

gpsGateMaxSecs.description: Give-up cap on the GPS/LTE gate in seconds. Default 600; 0 = no time cap (the other release conditions still apply).

gpsGateNoProgressSecs.description: No-progress escape hatch for the GPS/LTE gate, in seconds. Releases the gate once NEITHER a GPS fix NOR an LTE connection has arrived for this long — the underground-garage case, where every other release condition is blind. Cannot fire while LTE is connected (that is the genuinely-acquiring case). Default 120; 0 = off, leaving only gpsGateMaxSecs.

spawnStaggerSecs.description: Delay between camera encoder spawns in seconds (flattens the start-up power transient). Default 4; 0 = simultaneous.

cameras.description: Per-camera enable keyed by stream key (e.g. {"cam1": false}). A disabled camera gets no pipeline at all — no recording, no shm bridge, no live stream. An absent key means enabled, so {} is every detected camera (the default). Use it to match camera count to the supply (one camera on a 3 A install, two on 5 A).

mode.description: auto (default): drain segments to S3 whenever connected; off: keep local only.

uvSamples.description: Shed when this many ~1 Hz samples with the CURRENT undervoltage bit land within uvWindowSecs. Default 3.

uvWindowSecs.description: Undervoltage counting window in seconds. Default 30.

railLowVolts.description: Alternative trigger: 5 V rail below this, sustained railLowSecs. Default 4.85.

railLowSecs.description: How long the rail must stay below railLowVolts to trigger. Default 15.

escalateDwellSecs.description: Trailing window (seconds) evaluated for escalation to the next rung (no-live → bridge-only). Default 60.

escalateDutyPct.description: Escalate when the supply was bad (shed trigger, or an individual undervoltage/low-rail sample) for at least this percentage of the trailing escalateDwellSecs window. Default 70; 100 requires a continuously bad supply, which a noisy rail never provides.

cpuTempC.description: Thermal arm trigger: shed live streaming once the SoC has been at/above this for cpuTempSecs. Default 80 (5 °C below the Pi hard throttle).

cpuTempRestoreC.description: Thermal restore threshold: the SoC must be below this for the restore timer to run. Default 70 (a 10 °C anti-flap margin).

cpuTempSecs.description: How long the SoC must hold at/above cpuTempC to arm the shed. Default 15.

restoreSecs.description: Clean interval (zero undervoltage samples, rail at/above railRestoreVolts) required to restore one rung. Default 120.

railRestoreVolts.description: Rail must be at/above this for a sample to count as clean. Default 4.95.

maxShedsPerHour.description: Shed cycles per rolling hour before the device parks at its shed level (no auto-restore until reboot or a settings change). Default 4.

powerShedding.description: Runtime undervoltage + thermal load shedding: when the 5 V rail measurably fails (or the SoC runs hot), the device sheds live streaming first, then video recording (bridge-only), and restores in reverse with hysteresis. Telemetry recording is never shed.

maxBytes.description: Local recordings quota in bytes (oldest segments evicted first). Default 10 GiB.

minFreeBytes.description: Free-disk floor in bytes; recording evicts/stops before crossing it. Default 2 GiB.

RecordingConfig.description: On-device recording settings (`recording` namespace). All fields optional — omitted fields fall back to device defaults. Unknown keys and out-of-range values are rejected. Applied live by the agent (5 s settings poll, and forced on every cloud config message); toggling video recording or changing its preset briefly restarts the live stream.

gpsFixResetPolicy.description: With a live GPS fix: "defer" (default) allows a modem reset only after 30+ min of unusable LTE; "veto-deadzone" additionally never resets while parked in a dead zone.

deadZoneProfile.description: Dead-zone recovery pacing: conservative (nudge every 15-120 min, never resets), balanced (default; 10-60 min, reset only after 3 failed radio cycles), aggressive (10-20 min, reset after 1 failed cycle).

LteRecoveryConfig.description: LTE recovery policy (`lteRecovery` namespace): how aggressively the device connection manager may use the GNSS-destructive full modem reset. Both fields optional; omitted fields fall back to the device defaults. Read live by the modem daemon at its next recovery decision — no device restart.

offlineSources.description: Kill switch: false disables GPS/NITZ clock stepping entirely (device default: true).

stepThresholdSecs.description: Step only when the measured clock offset exceeds this many seconds (device default 10). A battery-backed RTC boots inside the threshold, making the feature a natural no-op.

maxStepsPerBoot.description: Hard cap on clock steps per boot (device default 4; bounds a flapping source).

TimeSyncConfig.description: Offline time sources (`timeSync` namespace): while NTP is unsynced this boot, the agent may step the system clock from GPS (valid GNSS fix) or the modem NITZ clock, then stand down for the boot once NTP synchronizes. All fields optional; omitted fields fall back to the device defaults.

apn.description: Access Point Name for the cellular data context. EMPTY or ABSENT leaves the modem's stored APN untouched — the safe default for every existing device. A change is applied with confirm-and-rollback: the device proves real data flows over the new APN within a bounded window, or restores the previous one by itself.

CellularConfig.description: Cellular data-context settings (`cellular` namespace). `apn` empty or absent leaves the modem's stored APN untouched (the safe default). A non-empty APN is applied by the modem daemon with apply-and-confirm rollback: real traffic must flow over the modem interface within a bounded window or the previous APN is restored automatically. Read live from settings.json by the modem daemon — never restart it to apply a setting.

rotationDeg.description: Rotation applied at the sensor, degrees. 180 = the camera is mounted upside down, so the sensor flips H+V and every consumer (live WebRTC, recorded MP4s, replays, workflow frames) sees an upright image with no added CPU. Only 0 and 180 exist — the camera overlay parameter has no 90/270.

cameras.description: Per-camera mounting rotation keyed by stream key, e.g. {"cam0": {"rotationDeg": 180}}. An ABSENT key is UNMANAGED: the device leaves that camera's boot config exactly as it found it. Send an explicit {"rotationDeg": 0} to take a camera over and force it upright. Takes effect on the next boot — the device reports `rebootRequired` and never reboots itself.

CameraMountConfig.description: Camera mounting rotation (`cameraMount` namespace): per-camera 0/180 applied at the image sensor via the camera overlay in /boot/firmware/config.txt, so live video, recordings, replays and workflow frames are all corrected at zero CPU cost. ⚠️ Applies on the NEXT BOOT: the agent edits the boot config and reports the namespace with a `rebootRequired` detail; it never reboots the device itself. An absent camera key is unmanaged (the boot config is left as found); an explicit `rotationDeg: 0` forces that camera upright.

scenarioId.description: Catalog id of the scenario to replay (demo-assets/v1/<scenarioId>/).

loop.description: Replay the scenario again after the parked gap; false parks at the end of the lap until changed.

SimulationConfig.description: Device-simulator scenario selection (`simulation` namespace). Accepted only for devices created as simulated; a simulated device replays the catalog scenario `scenarioId` from `demo-assets/v1/`, parks for `gapSeconds` between laps, and loops while `loop` is true. Applied live by the replay source (5 s settings poll, and forced on every cloud config message); a changed scenarioId ends the current lap in place.

enabled.description: OBD polling kill switch. false (default) keeps the helper stopped and the vehicle card in its "not configured" state; true starts polling once an adapter is set.

adapterMac.description: Bluetooth MAC of the ELM327 adapter (AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF, stored uppercase). null = no adapter configured; the device never pairs by name, so this is the only way it learns which dongle is its own.

pin.description: Pairing PIN for a legacy-pairing adapter, 4 to 6 digits (default 1234). Ignored by SSP adapters.

pollHz.description: Poll cycles per second, 0.2 to 2 (default 1). One cycle reads every configured field once.

fields.description: Fields to poll, a subset of the model's declared `peripherals.obd.fields`. Empty (default) = every field the model declares. The device skips any field the vehicle does not support regardless.

powerSource.description: How the tracker device itself is powered, NOT the adapter (the vehicle's OBD port powers the adapter either way). "switched" (default): the device sits on a 12 V socket that dies with the ignition, so polling simply ends when the device loses power; the helper only needs to stop cleanly when the ECU goes silent. "constant": the device is hardwired, always on; the helper stops polling when the ECU goes silent and additionally pauses below 11.8 V, resuming above 12.4 V, so it can never drain the battery.

ObdConfig.description: Vehicle OBD-II adapter settings (`obd` namespace). Accepted only for devices whose model declares `peripherals.obd` (400 otherwise). Every field is optional and an omitted field falls back to the device default, but the namespace is replaced WHOLE on write (send the fields you want to keep). `adapterMac` names the ELM327 Bluetooth adapter the device pairs with (stored uppercase; the device never pairs by name), `enabled` is the polling kill switch, `fields` narrows the polled set below the model's declared list (empty = all), and `powerSource` says how the tracker device (not the adapter) is powered, which selects the battery policy. Applied live by the agent's OBD collector on its settings poll and on every cloud config message; a changed adapter restarts the helper. Pairing outcome, probe profile and scan candidates come back in the config report under `effective.obd`.

sensor.description: The image sensor on this port: an id of the camera catalog (camera-catalog.json, `sensors[].id`), or "none" for a port declared empty. The catalog, not this schema, is the list of valid ids, so that adding a sensor does not change the config contract. An id the catalog does not list is a 400 naming the ones it does.

options.description: Per-board overlay parameters of the chosen sensor, by the option keys the catalog lists for it (`sensors[].options[].key`), each set to one of that option's `values`. An option left out uses the overlay default. Not allowed with "sensor": "none".

cameras.description: Per-port sensor declaration keyed by stream key, e.g. {"cam0": {"sensor": "imx708"}, "cam1": {"sensor": "none"}}. An ABSENT key is UNMANAGED: the device leaves that port's camera line in /boot/firmware/config.txt exactly as it found it. A key must be a camera port the device's model declares. Takes effect on the next boot: the device reports that a reboot is required and never reboots itself.

CameraSensorsConfig.description: Camera sensor per port (`cameraSensors` namespace): which image sensor is attached to each camera port of this device, keyed by stream key. `sensor` is an id of the camera catalog or "none" for an empty port; `options` are that sensor's per-board overlay parameters. The agent makes the port's `dtoverlay=` line in /boot/firmware/config.txt match. ⚠️ Applies on the NEXT BOOT: the agent edits the boot config and reports that a reboot is required; it never reboots the device itself. An absent port key is unmanaged (the line is left as found). Accepted only for a real (not simulated) device running the Rust agent that either has not reported yet or advertises the `camera.sensors` capability; otherwise a 400 naming the agent version needed. Replaced WHOLE on write, so send every port you want to keep managed.

DeviceConfig.description: The consolidated device config document (`devices.config`). One key per namespace, all optional: an ABSENT namespace means the device uses its own defaults. Namespace keys are the wire/settings.json keys and are never renamed. Published verbatim (plus `v`, `rev`, `uploadBucket`, `ts`) as a retained MQTT message on `xorgate/devices/{id}/config`.

activeStreamsViewType.description: Layout for the Active Streams tab: card grid (default) or location-first map view.

azimuthDeg.description: Camera azimuth for the 3D orientation view, degrees.

elevationDeg.description: Camera elevation for the 3D orientation view, degrees. Bounded to ±85: at the poles the look-at up-vector degenerates and the view flips.

DeviceUiPrefs.description: Cloud-only presentation preferences (`devices.ui_prefs`). NEVER delivered to the device and never bumps `configRev`. Absent keys fall back to {"activeStreamsViewType":"card","imuView":{"azimuthDeg":45,"elevationDeg":24}}.

DeviceIdentity.description: The device's AWS IoT X.509 identity, non-secret fields only. `certificateArn` and `credentialEndpoint` are deliberately withheld, and the private key is never stored server-side at all (it is returned exactly once, at provisioning time).

iotThingName.description: Equals the device id, and is also the MQTT client id.

roleAlias.description: IoT role alias the device assumes for KVS + S3 access.

DeviceRegistrationCameras.description: A camera sensor per port, keyed by stream key (`cam0`, `cam1`): the `cameras` map of the `cameraSensors` config namespace (see `CameraSensorsConfig`), validated by the same rules. `sensor` is an id of the camera catalog or "none" for an empty port; `options` are that sensor's per-board overlay parameters.

sensor.description: A camera catalog sensor id, or "none" for a port with no camera.

options.description: Option values by the keys the catalog lists for the sensor. Not allowed with "none".

DeviceRegistration.description: A short-lived onboarding code. The operator runs `installUrl` on the device; the install script claims the code, which creates the device row and provisions its IoT identity.

code.description: The registration code, unique across the platform.

status.description: A stale `pending` row flips to `expired` lazily, when it is read, and there is no sweeper, so a code can be past `expiresAt` and still read `pending` until someone fetches it.

deviceId.description: The device created by the claim; null until then.

expiresAt.description: 15 minutes after the code was minted.

installUrl.description: The one-liner target: `<api base>/get/{code}`, which serves the install script. That route is internal to the installer and is not part of the public API.

cameras.description: Present on `rust` registrations only; a `js` registration has no such key. The camera sensor chosen per port, which the claim stores as the new device's `cameraSensors` config namespace when the installer declares the `camera.sensors` capability. null = no choice was made: the device starts on its model's own sensors. The claim does not change this field, so it shows what was chosen, not what was applied.

SearchResult.description: One hit, normalized across resource types so a caller renders any of them from one code path. `id` addresses the resource of that `type`.

type.description: The workflow types are returned by the endpoint but their resources are not part of this documented API surface yet.

title.description: Device name (falling back to serial), or template name.

MediaSession.description: A continuous on-device recording run for one camera (offline recording plan). Sessions are per-camera: a dual-camera drive is two sessions with near-identical startedAt. `status` is advisory: a session closes ~10 min after segments stop arriving and reopens if a straggler segment lands later.

timeSource.description: Device clock quality at session start; "unsynced" timestamps may be wrong wall-clock. "gps"/"nitz" = offline clock step from GNSS / modem NITZ time while NTP was pending.

lastSegmentAt.description: Server-side arrival time of the most recent segment (upload can lag recording).

clockCorrectionMs.description: Clock-step correction: the cumulative forward shift (ms) the server applied to this session's segments because the device recorded them on a stale boot clock (no RTC) that NTP/GPS/NITZ later stepped. startedAt/endedAt and the segment startTs values are already corrected. NULL = never corrected.

thumbnailKey.description: S3 key of the poster frame extracted from the first segment. NULL when none exists (pre-feature session, first segment never uploaded, or extraction failed) — always treat as optional. Not fetchable directly; use `thumbnailUrl`.

thumbnailUrl.description: Presigned GET for the poster frame JPEG (list endpoint only, same TTL as segment playback URLs). NULL when the session has no thumbnail.

RecordingRun.description: One drive, as a human means it: the media sessions whose intervals are within 60 s of each other, clustered server-side. A session that is still open has no endedAt, so its interval end is estimated as startedAt + the duration uploaded so far, which means an open run's toTs grows as its backlog drains.

key.description: The earliest member session's id, a stable identity across polls. (There is no run row in the database and no device-side run id.)

fromTs.description: Earliest member startedAt. With toTs, the run's composite-replay window.

streamKeys.description: Every camera that recorded in this run, sorted.

anyOpen.description: Some member may still be receiving segments.

anyUnsynced.description: Some member recorded with an unsynchronized device clock.

sessions.description: The members, ordered by startedAt then streamKey.

MediaSegment.description: One ~60 s MP4 segment of a media session. `finalized: false` = crash-cut partial (fragmented MP4, playable up to the cut). When stitching, prefer the next segment's startTs delta over durationMs (segment 0 includes ~2 s pipeline startup). Ingest drops segments whose startTs is more than MEDIA_SEGMENT_MAX_FUTURE_MS (default 24 h) ahead of server time: a device with a catastrophically wrong clock is rejected loudly rather than indexed where no query will find it.

ReplayManifest.description:
Everything a replay player needs in one response: per-session gap-aware timelines plus a presigned GET URL per segment. All timestamps are epoch milliseconds (the replay-clock unit), unlike the ISO strings elsewhere in this API. Format-neutral by design: no codec strings or playlist syntax, so clients parse media details from the segment bytes.

Since API 0.9.0 it also carries `telemetry`: the recorded-telemetry sessions overlapping the replay window, as presigned S3 artifacts (see the schema). Omitted only when the request said `telemetry=0`; a server older than 0.9.0 never sends it, so treat it as optional.

from.description: Epoch ms start of the whole replay: the requested range (range mode) or the earliest covered instant incl. any evicted-head gap (session mode).

to.description: Epoch ms end of the whole replay.

urlExpiresAt.description: Epoch ms after which segment URLs may stop working (real TTL minus a safety margin). Refetch the manifest before this.

sessions.description: One entry per session with media in the replay (a dual-camera range yields two). A sessionId request whose segments have all expired returns the session with empty segments/gaps, for telemetry-only replay.

timeSource.description: "unsynced" = wall-clock correlation with telemetry is untrustworthy; "gps"/"nitz" = offline clock step while NTP was pending.

clockCorrectionMs.description: Cumulative forward shift (ms) applied to this session for a device clock step (see `MediaSession.clockCorrectionMs`); the timeline is already corrected. NULL = never corrected; absent from servers older than 0.19.0.

segments.description: Ordered by startTs. Segment i covers [startTs, startTs + effectiveDurationMs).

effectiveDurationMs.description: Next-segment startTs delta when contiguous, else the recorded durationMs. Deltas beat durations (rotation timestamps are accurate; durations drift). A recorded durationMs is capped at the nominal segment length + 10 s, so a segment inflated by an uncorrected device clock step never bridges the step (the remainder becomes a missing-segments gap).

finalized.description: False = crash-cut partial; playable up to the cut.

anchor.description: startTs provenance. "fstat" seq-0 rows include ~2 s of pipeline startup, so the first seam may hold a ~2 s buffered hole.

url.description: Presigned S3 GET for the MP4.

gaps.description: Holes > 2 s with no media, computed server-side so every client renders the same timeline; the replay clock free-runs (or skips) across them.

ReplayTelemetry.description: Recorded telemetry for the replay window, served as immutable S3 artifacts by presigned URL (telemetry session artifacts). A **telemetry session** is a different id from a video session: both are minted independently on the device, so they are joined by TIME, not by id. This block lists every telemetry session with at least one segment overlapping `replay.from`..`replay.to`, in start order (a session whose bounds straddle the window but whose data sits in a recording hole is not listed). A device with recording off, or nothing recorded in the window, returns `{ "sessions": [], "truncated": false }`. Every URL here shares `replay.urlExpiresAt` with the video URLs, so one refetch refreshes all of them.

truncated.description: True when the window contained more than 1,500 telemetry segments (about 24 hours at the default 60 s rotation) and only the earliest 1,500 by `startTs` are listed. Not an error: narrow the window to reach the rest. The cap is separate from the 600 video segments, which are still a 400.

ReplayTelemetrySession.description: One telemetry session overlapping the replay window. Two tiers of artifact: `overview` is the precomputed, downsampled `overview.v1` object (route line, scrub preview, every metric, gzipped columnar JSON, typically 15 to 40 KB), and `segments` are the raw 60 s files the device recorded, clipped to the window. All timestamps epoch ms.

id.description: Device-minted UUIDv7 of the TELEMETRY session.

status.description: Advisory, same rule as media sessions: `closed` about 10 minutes after segments stop arriving; a straggler segment reopens it and the overview is rebuilt on the next close.

rateHz.description: Sample rate the device recorded at.

timeSource.description: The WORST clock quality seen across the session's segment headers. `rtc` is common on a boot that never synced; `unsynced` means wall-clock correlation with video is untrustworthy.

from.description: Epoch ms of the first sample in the session (not clipped to the window).

to.description: Epoch ms of the last sample in the session so far.

overview.description: `null` while the session is `open`, and for a short while after it closes until the artifact is built. A client then builds its own overview from `segments`, which is cheap (about 5 KB per minute recorded), and polls the manifest about every 60 s while any session is open.

segments.description: Only the segments overlapping the replay window, ordered by `startTs`. Each is the device's own gzipped JSONL file, served with `Content-Encoding: gzip` so `fetch()` inflates it natively: a header line, then one `{ ts, mono, seq, metrics }` sample per line. Immutable and safe to cache by URL path.

insights.description: The session's insights, byte-identical to the block inside the overview object. `null` until the overview has been built.

format.description: The artifact format. Additive fields keep `overview.v1`; a breaking change is a new format name, and this field says which one the URL serves.

bytes.description: Gzipped size, for fetch budgeting. `null` for an artifact built before sizes were recorded.

seq.description: Device sequence within the session. Order by `startTs`, never by `seq`.

startTs.description: Epoch ms of the first sample IN THE FILE.

endTs.description: Epoch ms of the last sample in the file.

samples.description: Valid sample lines in the file.

TelemetryInsights.description: Per-session summaries computed from the segments when the overview is built, one namespace per insight. Versioned PER INSIGHT: `computed` maps each insight id to the version that produced it, so a consumer can tell `distance` v1 from a future v2 without a format bump. Additive: new insight ids appear as new keys, so read the ones you know and ignore the rest. A scalar that could not be computed is `{ "value": null, "reason": ... }`. Every insight is a pure function of the recorded segments (nothing that depends on a geofence, an org setting or a model), which is what makes a rebuild reproducible. The v1 set: `duration`, `distance`, `speed`, `position`, `altitude`, `gpsQuality`, `system`, `lte`, `stops` (an event list) and, for a device whose model declares `peripherals.obd`, `vehicle` (OBD-II: engine-on and idle time, rpm and coolant maxima, fuel start/end/used with refuel events, odometer start/end/delta as a GPS cross-check, DTC events, live-link time; present only when `obd.link` reached 2 in the session) and, for a device that reports `system.led_state`, `deviceStatus` (time per status-LED code and per health flag, the worst code, and the contiguous LED-state intervals). See the platform-concepts page on telemetry sessions for each block's fields.

computed.description: `{ insightId: version }` for every insight present.

distance.description: `meters` by haversine over ACCEPTED fixes, with the acceptance rule (`accept`), the fix counts, and `crossCheckMeters` (the integral of `gps.speed` over the same fixes). A large disagreement between the two marks a suspect trace.

vehicle.description: OBD-II summary, gated on `obd.link === 2` (ECU answering). `link.liveMs`; `engineOn.ms` (`obd.rpm > 0`); `idle.ms` (engine on and `obd.speed`, else `gps.speed`, at or under `movingThresholdKph`; `speedSource` says which); `rpm.max` + `maxAt`; `coolant.max` (C); `fuel.startPct/endPct/usedPct` (`usedPct = max(0, start - end)`, so a session with a refuel reads 0: check `refuels`); `odometer.startKm/endKm/deltaKm` (`role: cross-check`, never the distance); `dtc.maxCount/endCount/milEnd/events`; `truncated` when an event kind hit its 50 cap. Each sub-block is `{ value: null, reason }` when its metric was never seen while live. Refuel (`fromPct`, `toPct`) and DTC (`count`) findings are in `events`.

deviceStatus.description: What the kit's status LED showed, from the 1 Hz `system.led_state` code (severity-ascending: 0 healthy, 1 starting, 2 gps_wait, 3 network, 4 thermal, 5 undervoltage, 6 agent_down reserved) and `system.health_flags` bitmask (1 undervoltage, 2 thermal, 4 lte_down, 8 mqtt_down, 16 gps_no_fix, 32 gps_gate_hold, 64 dead_zone, 128 power_shed, 256 live_block). `version` (1); `worstCode`; `byCodeMs` (code -> ms, every code "0".."6" present); `byFlagMs` (bit value -> ms the bit was set, every known bit present); `events`, the contiguous LED-state runs `{ kind: "led_state", ts, endTs, value }` with sub-2 s blips folded into a neighbour, at most 500 (the longest kept, `truncated: true`). A sample holds until the next one, at most 10 s. Present only when the session carries `system.led_state`. These intervals live in this block, not in the top-level `events`.

events.description: Timestamped findings (`stop`; `refuel` with `fromPct`/`toPct` and `dtc` with `count` from the `vehicle` insight), bounded per kind, so a timeline can pin them and a click can seek. Never a per-sample series.

kind.description: `stop`, `refuel` or `dtc` in v1; more may follow.

TelemetryWindowInsights.description: Distance, moving time and (for an OBD-II device) the vehicle roll-up inside a window (GET /devices/{id}/telemetry/insights).

sessions.description: The telemetry sessions overlapping the window, oldest first.

overlapMs.description: Milliseconds of the window the session's bounds cover.

source.description: `overview`: numbers from the built artifact. `unbuilt`: no artifact yet, numbers null.

distanceM.description: Metres inside the window; 0 when built but nothing moved.

fixes.description: Overview points inside the window with an accepted fix.

vehicle.description: Null when unbuilt, or when the overview has no `obd` grid with a live bucket inside the window.

distanceM.description: Sum over the built sessions; null when none is built.

telemetryMs.description: Milliseconds of the window covered by any session (union).

partial.description: At least one overlapping session has no built overview yet.

vehicle.description: Roll-up over the sessions that have one: `liveMs`, `engineOnMs`, `idleMs`, `fuelUsedPct`, `odometerDeltaKm`, `refuels` and `dtcEvents` are SUMMED; `rpmMax` and `coolantMax` are the MAX. Fuel and odometer start/end values and the event lists are per session only (read the session insight). Null when no session has one.

TelemetryWindowVehicle.description: The `vehicle` insight's rules run over an overview's `obd` grid clipped to the window (`method: "overview-obd"`): gated on `obd.link === 2`, legs broken at 30 s, bucket-averaged so within one bucket width of the raw-sample session insight.

engineOnMs.description: `obd.rpm > 0`; null when the vehicle reports no rpm.

idleMs.description: Engine on and not moving (`obd.speed`, else `gps.speed`); null without a speed.

fuelUsedPct.description: `max(0, first - last)` of `obd.fuel_level` inside the window.

odometerDeltaKm.description: `last - first` of `obd.odometer` inside the window: a GPS cross-check, never the distance.

refuels.description: Rises of `obd.fuel_level` over 5 points between consecutive buckets.

TelemetrySession.description: One recorded-telemetry session as the index knows it: lifecycle, counters and the `insights` mirror, with NO URLs (the replay manifest presigns). Timestamps are ISO-8601 here, like the media sessions list; the manifest's epoch-ms exception does not apply.

lastSegmentAt.description: Server-side arrival time of the newest segment: the close-detection clock.

overviewBytes.description: Gzipped size of the overview; `null` until built or backfilled.

clockCorrectionMs.description: Clock-step correction: the cumulative forward shift (ms) the server applied to samples the device stamped on a stale boot clock (no RTC) before NTP/GPS/NITZ stepped it. `from`/`to` and the stored samples are already corrected. `null` = never corrected.

insights.description: `null` until the overview has been built.

DeviceProvisioning.description: One-shot credential bundle returned by POST /devices/{id}/provision. certificatePem and privateKey are shown only here and are never stored server-side.

thingName.description: AWS IoT thing name (equals the device id).

dataEndpoint.description: AWS IoT Core data endpoint (iot:Data-ATS); MQTT over mTLS on port 8883.

credentialEndpoint.description: AWS IoT credential-provider endpoint used with the role alias to obtain short-lived AWS creds.

roleAlias.description: IoT role alias the device assumes for KVS + S3 access.

privateKey.description: Device private key (PEM). Shown once, never stored.

channels.description: One signaling channel per declared video stream.

VideoChannel.description: One live video channel a viewer can join.

channelRef.description: Opaque handle for the channel. Pass it back to the SDK; do not parse it. The value happens to be an ARN today and that is not part of the contract.

TelemetryReading.description: One telemetry reading (raw) or one downsample bucket (when `interval` was given; `value` is then the bucket average and `ts` the bucket start).

TelemetryTableColumn.description: One column of the history table. The array order IS the column order, and every row's `v` array is positional against it.

unit.description: Taken from device_latest, so it is stable across pages rather than scraped from whatever this page happened to contain. Null when the metric has no known unit.

TelemetryTableRow.description: One sample: a timestamp and its values. `v` is POSITIONAL against `columns` and its length always equals `columns.length`, and trailing nulls are never trimmed.

v.description: null means no reading for that column at this timestamp.

DeviceLatest.description: The most recent reading for one (device, metric) pair.

Author.description: The person a row is attributed to. When the account behind it was deleted the fields degrade to `{"id": "", "name": "Unknown user", "email": ""}` rather than to null.

WorkflowTemplateTag.description: A free-form label, normalized on write: trimmed, lowercased and deduplicated, 1 to 32 characters matching `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]*$`, at most 20 per template. A value that cannot be normalized into that shape is a 400 rather than a silent drop.

WorkflowTemplate.description: The list-row view of an org-scoped workflow template. The graph itself is not here: it lives on the template's versions, which only the detail response carries.

slug.description: Derived from the name at creation and unique within the organization. Stable: it does not follow a rename.

tags.description: Always present; an untagged template has an empty array.

currentVersion.description: The highest version number, published or not.

publishedVersion.description: null until the template has been published once.

usedBy.description: How many devices this template is attached to.

requiredCapabilities.description: Abstract input needs derived from the graph that would run (the published version, else the current one): tokens such as `video`, `gps`, `metric:<key>`. A device lacking one of them is refused on attach.

WorkflowTemplateVersion.description: One saved graph. At most one `draft` and one `published` row per template.

definition.description: The graph, as `{ schemaVersion, nodes, edges }`. Its format is documented at https://docs.xorgate.io/docs/workflows/definitions and is a frozen contract shared with `@xorgate/workflow-engine`. Served upgraded to the current schema version, whatever the stored row holds.

storedSchemaVersion.description: The schema version of the STORED row, before the read-path upgrade.

WorkflowTemplateDeployment.description: One device this template is attached to.

id.description: The attachment id, not the device id.

name.description: The device's name, falling back to its serial.

count.description: Templates in this organization carrying the tag.

DevicePurgeScope.description: `workflows`: attached workflows, their production runs and artifacts. `telemetry`: recorded telemetry sessions and every stored reading. `media`: recorded video sessions and thumbnails.

scopes.description: Which kinds of data to remove. Duplicates are ignored.

DevicePurgeCounts.description: What the purge has removed so far. Every key is present once the job has started; scopes that were not requested stay at 0.

runObjects.description: S3 objects under the deleted runs.

status.description: `queued` until a worker picks it up, `running` while it walks its steps, then `succeeded` or `failed` (see `error`). A failed purge may have removed part of the data; `counts` says how much, and a new purge picks up the rest.

cutoff.description: Data older than this is removed; uploads after it are kept.

cursor.description: Where the job is. `step` is one of `workflows.attachments`, `workflows.stop`, `workflows.runs`, `telemetry.s3`, `telemetry.sessions`, `telemetry.ingestLog`, `telemetry.readings`, `media.s3`, `media.sessions`, `done`; the other keys are the step's own position and are not a stable contract.

requestedBy.description: User id or API key id of the principal that asked.

leaseUntil.description: Worker lease. Operational detail; clients read `status` and `stalled`.

stalled.description: True when the purge is `running` but no worker has renewed its lease for over 30 minutes: the job died mid-way. A new `POST` closes it and starts over.

runs.description: Production runs the purge would delete.

readingsFrom.description: Oldest stored reading, or null when there are none.

limit.description: How many of the newest messages to return. Out-of-range numbers are clamped to 1..50; a non-number is a 400 (`VALIDATION_ERROR`).

id.description: Storage and index of each part joined by `+` (e.g. `SM:3+SM:4`). Stable within one read only.

storage.description: Store of the first part: SIM (`SM`) or modem (`ME`).

from.description: Sender as decoded; alphanumeric senders verbatim.

sentAt.description: Service-centre timestamp with its own UTC offset, or null if undecodable.

unread.description: Unread on the SIM. Reading does not change it.

text.description: Decoded text; a hex string when `binary`.

incomplete.description: A concatenated message with parts missing.

storage.description: Used and total slots per store that answered (`SM`, `ME`).

total.description: Messages on the device after joining parts, before the limit.

skipped.description: Stored items that were not readable messages.

partial.description: The device ran out of time; fewer messages than stored.

cleared.description: Clears only (`action: "clear"`): how many messages each store (`SM`, `ME`) held before the delete. The rest of the result is the device's sweep after the delete, normally empty.

status.description: `pending` until the device answers (usually within a few seconds), then `ok` or `error`. A read still pending after 45 s is reported as `expired`; a reply that arrives later still lands.

errorCode.description: Why it failed: the device's status (`no_modem`, `no_sim`, `modem_busy`, `error`), `timeout` on expiry, or `publish_failed` when the command never reached the broker.

errorMessage.description: The device's own error detail, if any.

action.description: `read` (`POST /devices/{id}/sms-reads`) or `clear` (`POST /devices/{id}/sms/clear`). A clear is polled and stored like a read; its `result` is the device's state after the delete, plus `cleared`.

requestedBy.description: User id or API key id of the principal that asked.

TransferAdoption.description: Whether the DEVICE has confirmed it is now publishing under the new tenancy. `pending` is the normal answer immediately after a transfer and is not an error: the ownership change is already complete and authoritative in the cloud, and the device adopts it from the retained config on its next connect. `unknown` means the device has never reported a telemetry scope at all — every agent older than v0.0.6 is in this state — and must NOT be read as "not scoped". Read it back from `GET /devices/{id}`; a scope change deliberately does not move the config revision, so the revision is not evidence either way.

id.description: The transfer record, for audit and support.

crossOrg.description: True when the destination workspace belongs to a different organization.

detachedWorkflowAttachments.description: Template names whose attachments were removed by the cross-organization sweep. Always empty for a same-organization move.

kvsChannelsRetagged.description: Video signaling channels re-tagged to the new tenancy.

scopeAttributes.description: What happened to the IoT thing attributes that authorize the device's telemetry topic. `failed` is a DEGRADED SUCCESS: the device moved and was told its new topic, but the broker was not told to allow it, so it publishes on the legacy (still-ingested) telemetry plane until any setting save re-asserts the attributes. Workspace-scoped credentials cannot see its telemetry meanwhile.

warnings.description: Human-readable notes about what this transfer did and did not do — an offline device, detached workflows, history travelling with the device, session tokens that lose sight of it. Surface these; none of them is an error.

workflowAttachments.description: Attachments the cross-organization sweep would DETACH, named so a confirmation dialog can show them before the operator agrees rather than after. Their templates belong to the source organization and the destination cannot see them.

runningWorkflowRuns.description: Runs executing right now. They are left to finish; their history is stamped with the organization that started them.

openMediaSessions.description: Recording sessions still accepting uploads. They keep uploading — segments are keyed by device, not by tenant.

staleSessionTokens.description: Live workspace-scoped session tokens naming the SOURCE workspace. They stop seeing the device and are NOT revoked.

carriesHistory.description: Always true, and stated rather than implied. Every historical telemetry reading and every recorded segment is stored against the device and MOVES WITH IT. Nothing is purged. For a cross-organization transfer that is a data-disclosure event and the confirmation must say so.

blockers.description: Non-empty means the transfer would be refused. Returned rather than thrown so the dialog can explain the refusal; `POST .../transfer` turns the first of them into its 400 or 409.

TransferOffer.description: An offer as its SENDER (or, once accepted, its recipient) sees it.

code.description: The redemption code. A secret — anyone holding it can accept or decline.

direction.description: `outgoing` when your organization created the offer, `incoming` when it accepted one.

workspaceId.description: Where the device sat when the offer was created.

TransferOfferPreview.description: An offer as its RECIPIENT sees it, holding nothing but the code. The fields here are the whole allowlist: enough to decide whether to accept, and no more. The device id, serial, workspace, configuration and telemetry are all deliberately absent — whoever holds the code is not yet entitled to the device.

willDetachWorkflowAttachments.description: Workflow template names this device is attached to. If a DIFFERENT organization accepts the offer they are all detached, because the templates belong to yours. Shown at creation because the sender is not present at acceptance.

Unauthorized.description: No usable credential. `UNAUTHORIZED` for a missing, malformed or expired bearer token; `INVALID_API_KEY`, `API_KEY_REVOKED` or `API_KEY_EXPIRED` for an `xg_` key that does not verify; `INVALID_SESSION_TOKEN`, `SESSION_TOKEN_REVOKED` or `SESSION_TOKEN_EXPIRED` for an `xgs_` token that does not (revoked also covers a token whose minting key was revoked or deleted, and expired covers one whose key expired — the holder cannot act on the key either way, so the token-shaped code is the useful one); `USER_CREDENTIAL_REQUIRED` when a key or a token was sent to an operation that needs a signed-in user; and `API_KEY_REQUIRED` on `POST /auth/session-tokens`, which takes only a key.

Forbidden.description: Not a member of the requested organization (`FORBIDDEN`), a member of none (`NO_ORGANIZATION`), or a member without the required role (`INSUFFICIENT_ROLE`). An API key sent with an `X-Organization-Id` other than its own is `FORBIDDEN`, and a key whose `role` is below the operation is `INSUFFICIENT_ROLE`. A workspace-scoped session token adds two of its own, neither of which a role can satisfy: `WORKSPACE_MISMATCH` for an `X-Workspace-Id` that contradicts the token, and `WORKSPACE_SCOPED` for an operation that is organization-wide.

NotFound.description: No such resource, or it belongs to another organization. Cross-tenant reads are deliberately indistinguishable from missing ones (`NOT_FOUND`).

BadRequest.description: Invalid body or query parameters (`BAD_REQUEST`), or a multi-organization caller who omitted `X-Organization-Id` (`ORGANIZATION_REQUIRED`).

Conflict.description: The resource is in a state that refuses this operation (`CONFLICT`).

MethodNotAllowed.description: The path exists but not with this method (`METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED`). The response carries an `Allow` header listing the methods this path does accept.

MeUser.description: The caller's profile after the write.

DeviceCommandAccepted.description: Command published to the device. Delivery to the broker only. The device may still reject it as expired or already-executed, and the real outcome is observed via device status.

requestId.description: Replay key. The device refuses to execute the same one twice.

expiresAt.description: Epoch ms after which the device refuses the command.

DeviceCommandPublishFailed.description: Delivering the command to the device failed (`COMMAND_PUBLISH_FAILED`). Retry.

get.summary: Current user, memberships, and organizations
get.description:
The bootstrap call. It resolves the bearer token to a user (creating the row on first sight) and returns every organization the caller belongs to, which is how a client learns what to put in `X-Organization-Id`. `memberships` are the plain rows, not the enriched roster shape that `GET /memberships` returns. This is the only org-aware endpoint that never needs the tenancy header.

**Cognito ID token only.** An `xg_` API key is refused here with `401 USER_CREDENTIAL_REQUIRED`: this operation describes a person, and a key has no user behind it.

organizations.description: Empty for a brand-new user. Create one with `POST /organizations` before calling anything org-scoped.

delete.description:
Closes the account for good: the Cognito user (so the email can sign up again from nothing), the profile row and picture, every organization membership, and the browser live-plane policy. Organizations the caller merely belonged to are untouched; device registrations they created keep a null creator.

Refused with `409 OWNS_ORGANIZATIONS` while the caller is the ONLY owner of any organization — the response lists them under `details.organizations`. Hand ownership to another member first (`PATCH /memberships/{id}` with `role: "owner"`) or delete the organization (`DELETE /organizations/{id}`). Several owners are allowed, so an owner who is not the last one is not blocked.

The ID token that made this call stays verifiable until it expires, but every later request with it is refused with `401 ACCOUNT_DELETED` rather than re-creating the profile. There is no undo.

**Cognito ID token only.** An `xg_` API key is refused with `401 USER_CREDENTIAL_REQUIRED`: this operation acts on a person, and a key has no user behind it.

409.description: The caller is the sole owner of at least one organization (`OWNS_ORGANIZATIONS`); `details.organizations` lists `{id, name, slug}` for each.

patch.description:
Sets the display name on the caller's `users` row. `null` clears it, and clients fall back to the email address. Nothing else about a user is editable here: the email is the Cognito sign-in and the tier and platform role are not self-service.

The name is NOT written back to the Cognito `name` attribute. That attribute seeds the row the first time a token is seen and has no reader afterwards; this row is the profile.

**Cognito ID token only.** An `xg_` API key is refused with `401 USER_CREDENTIAL_REQUIRED`: this operation acts on a person, and a key has no user behind it.

name.description: Trimmed before storing. `null` clears the name.

put.description:
The image arrives as base64 in the body rather than through a presigned PUT: clients downscale to a 512px square first, so the payload is tens of kilobytes and one round trip writes both the object and the row that points at it.

The declared `contentType` is checked against the bytes themselves — a payload whose magic number disagrees with its label is refused, because the declared type is what gets served back on the presigned GET. The stored object is private; the response carries a fresh `avatarUrl` for it.

**Cognito ID token only.** An `xg_` API key is refused with `401 USER_CREDENTIAL_REQUIRED`: this operation acts on a person, and a key has no user behind it.

contentType.description: Must match what the bytes actually are.

data.description: Base64 with no `data:` prefix. Decodes to at most 1.5 MB; larger is a 400.

delete.description:
Clears the picture; clients fall back to initials. Idempotent — a caller with no picture gets the same 200.

**Cognito ID token only.** An `xg_` API key is refused with `401 USER_CREDENTIAL_REQUIRED`: this operation acts on a person, and a key has no user behind it.

get.summary: List organizations the caller is a member of
get.description:
Paginated with the shared list dialect (a user belongs to a handful of organizations at most, so the default page size of 100 is effectively "all of them").

**Cognito ID token only.** The result is defined by the caller's memberships, which an API key does not have; a key is refused with `401 USER_CREDENTIAL_REQUIRED`. A key already knows its one organization.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Sort column. Anything else is a 400.

post.summary: Create a new organization and become its owner
post.description:
Bootstraps an organization for the caller and inserts a `memberships` row with `role: owner`. Does NOT require `X-Organization-Id` (the caller may have no orgs yet), which makes it the one write a brand-new user can perform.

**Cognito ID token only** (`401 USER_CREDENTIAL_REQUIRED` for an API key). The new organization needs an owner, and an owner is a user. This is a known limit for a consumer that wants to onboard its own customers programmatically: today it maps them onto WORKSPACES inside its one organization, which a default `member` key can create. Organizations for a consumer are provisioned out of band.

get.summary: Get the active organization
get.description: The `{id}` must be the ACTIVE organization (the one resolved from `X-Organization-Id` or from a sole membership). Reading a different organization you belong to means switching the header, not changing the path.

put.description: Partial update: send only the fields you want changed. An empty body is a 400, and targeting an organization other than the active one is a 403.

delete.description: Destroys the organization and everything under it: every workspace and every device (each torn down the way `DELETE /devices/{id}` is — IoT identity, video channels, uploaded media, telemetry), API keys and the session tokens minted from them, memberships, workflow templates, connector credentials in Secrets Manager, and the logos. Members whose only organization this was lose live-plane access. There is no undo and no soft-delete; a minimal deletion record (id, slug, counts, who, when) is kept.

put.description:
