The image arrives as base64 in the body rather than through a presigned PUT: clients fit it into a 512px square first, so the payload is tens of kilobytes and one round trip writes both the object and the row that points at it.

The declared `contentType` is checked against the bytes themselves — a payload whose magic number disagrees with its label is refused, because the declared type is what gets served back on the presigned GET. The stored object is private; the response carries a fresh `logoUrl` for it, and the previous object is deleted only after the row points at the new one.

Organization-wide, like every organization write: `{id}` must be the active organization, and a workspace-scoped session token gets `403 WORKSPACE_SCOPED`.

contentType.description: Must match what the bytes actually are.

data.description: Base64 with no `data:` prefix. Decodes to at most 1.5 MB; larger is a 400.

delete.description: Clears the logo; clients fall back to the initials of the name. Idempotent — an organization with no logo answers 200 with `logoUrl: null`.

get.summary: List members of the active organization
get.description: The roster, paginated with the shared list dialect (default order is ASCENDING by join date, the one list endpoint whose default is not `desc`). Each row is enriched with its member's `user` so a UI renders names and emails without a second round-trip.

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: Sort direction. Default `asc` here (join order), unlike other lists.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Sort column. Anything else is a 400.

200.description: List of memberships, each enriched with its member identity

post.summary: Add a user to the active organization (owner/admin only)
post.description: Adds a member by `userId` or `email`. If an `email` has no account yet, a Cognito account is provisioned and the invitee is emailed a temporary password to set on first sign-in; the invitation names this organization and the caller. `invited` is true when a new account was created and emailed. Someone who already has an account gets no credential, so they are emailed a notice that they were added instead. Either email is best-effort and never fails the request. Adding someone who is already a member is a 400, not a no-op.

schema.description: Provide either `userId` or `email` to identify the user.

201.description: Membership created (invitee provisioned + emailed when `invited` is true)

invited.description: True when a new Cognito account was created and emailed an invitation.

patch.description: Changes the role in place; before this existed the only way to change a role was to remove and re-invite the member. Two guards beyond the owner/admin gate: owner-level changes (granting `owner`, or changing an existing owner's role) need the caller to be an owner themselves, and demoting the LAST owner is refused with a 403 so an organization can never lock itself out. Setting the role a member already has is a no-op 200.

delete.summary: Remove a member, or leave the organization
delete.description:
Owners and admins can remove any member. Any member can remove THEIR OWN membership (leave); addressing someone else's with a lower role is a 403. Removing the last remaining owner is refused with a 403 either way, so an organization can never be left ownerless — hand ownership over first, or delete the organization.

Side effect: if this removal takes away the member's LAST organization membership, their live-plane access is revoked too (see `DELETE /live/access`), and any live subscription they hold dies on its next reconnect. Members who still belong to another organization keep live access.

get.summary: List API keys for the active organization
get.description: Paginated with the shared list dialect, newest first by default, and includes revoked and expired keys. The envelope key is `api_keys` (snake_case, mirroring the Postgres table name) while its contents are camelCase. That inconsistency is deliberate and stays on the wire; the SDKs present it as `apiKeys`. `keyPrefix` is null on keys minted before that column existed and cannot be recovered for them.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Sort column. Anything else is a 400.

200.description: API key metadata. The hashed key is never returned.

post.summary: Mint a new API key (owner/admin only)
post.description:
Returns the plaintext key exactly once, as `plaintext_key`. Only its SHA-256 is stored, so a lost key cannot be recovered, only replaced. Send the result as `Authorization: Bearer xg_...` to any organization-scoped operation in this document.

A key may not be minted more privileged than the caller minting it: an `admin` cannot mint an `owner` key (`403`), because that would be a one-step escalation to deleting the organization.

scope.description: Recorded on the key. Nothing enforces it yet.

role.description: The role the key acts with. Defaults to `member`, which is the right level for a data-plane consumer: it can register and manage devices and workspaces but cannot manage people, keys or the organization itself. Capped at the minting caller's own role.

expiresAt.description: Opt-in expiry, ISO-8601, must be in the future. Omit or send null for a key that never expires.

201.description: API key created. `plaintext_key` is shown only here.

plaintext_key.description: Save this. It is not retrievable later.

delete.summary: Permanently delete an API key (owner/admin only)
delete.description:
A hard delete, not a revocation: the row is removed and `revokedAt` is never used by this endpoint. The key stops authenticating immediately and thereafter reads as unknown (`401 INVALID_API_KEY`) rather than revoked. Rotation is therefore mint-then-delete, and a deleted key leaves no record of having existed.

**Every session token minted from this key dies with it, immediately.** That cascade is the emergency stop for a leaked browser credential: there is no per-token revoke endpoint, so if you need to end sessions now, delete the key they came from. Mint the replacement key first if you also need the integration to keep working.

post.summary: Exchange an API key for a short-lived session token
post.description:
Mints an `xgs_` **session token**: the only xorgate credential a browser or a mobile binary may hold. Call this from your SERVER, with your API key, after your own authorization decision about your own user. The token goes to the client; the key never leaves your infrastructure.

xorgate never learns who your user is. You authorize the person, xorgate authorizes the key, and `workspaceId` is how you express the first decision in terms the second one can enforce.

**API key only.** A Cognito ID token is `401 API_KEY_REQUIRED` (a signed-in session already authenticates this API directly and needs no exchange), and a session token cannot mint another one — otherwise a leaked token would renew itself forever and the expiry would mean nothing.

**The token is never more privileged than the key.** It inherits the key's `role`, and the role in force on any request is the LOWER of the token's and the key's CURRENT role, so downgrading a key downgrades its live tokens rather than leaving them privileged until they expire.

**`workspaceId` is enforced, not advisory.** Omit it and the token sees the whole organization, exactly as the key does. Supply it and the token is confined to that one workspace: device-scoped reads and writes are narrowed to it, an `X-Workspace-Id` header naming a different workspace is `403 WORKSPACE_MISMATCH`, and organization-wide operations (memberships, API keys, organization settings, workspace writes) answer `403 WORKSPACE_SCOPED` whatever the role. This is what lets you map your own customers onto workspaces and hand each of them a credential that cannot reach the others.

**Revocation.** Deleting the minting key with `DELETE /api-keys/{id}` destroys every token it minted, immediately. That is the emergency stop; there is no per-token revoke endpoint, because the maximum lifetime is an hour.

The response carries the live-plane coordinates alongside the token, so a client's entire configuration is the API base URL. The plaintext token is returned exactly once and only its SHA-256 is stored; there is no way to read it back.

201.description: Token minted. The plaintext is shown here and nowhere else.

post.summary: Vend credentials for the live plane, scoped to one tenant
post.description:
Returns the short-lived credentials the **live plane** is entered with. Live telemetry and live video are streaming protocols that this API does not carry, so they are not authorized by a bearer token the way the endpoints above are; they are entered with a signed connection, and this is what signs it.

**Treat the response as opaque.** Hand the object to the SDK and never read a field. The field names are dictated by the signing algorithm rather than chosen, which is exactly why they are not something to build against.

**Any credential may call this**, and which one you use is the difference between the two integration shapes. A session token is the DIRECT shape: your client holds the token and calls this itself. An API key is the PROXIED shape: your server calls this with the target `workspaceId` and hands the result to your client, which then touches no xorgate endpoint at all. A signed-in user session works too, and gets its organization.

**The scope is the boundary, on both planes.** Credentials vended for a workspace receive that workspace's devices' telemetry and can view that workspace's devices' video, and are refused a sibling workspace's — not filtered, refused, by the credential itself rather than by anything you have to remember to do. A workspace-scoped session token can only ever vend for its own workspace; anything else is `403 WORKSPACE_NOT_IN_SCOPE`.

**Lifetime is at most an hour and there is no refresh.** Cache what you get and mint again shortly before `expiration`; the SDK does this for you. There is no revoke endpoint, for the same reason session tokens have none — deleting the API key behind the credential is the emergency stop, and nothing vended survives an hour anyway.

**A device whose video has never been viewed under this scheme may need one extra call to become viewable**: the video plane is scoped by labels written onto the signalling channels, and vending is what reconciles them. If a channel comes back unviewable, vend again.

201.description: Credentials minted. Opaque; pass them to the SDK unread.

get.summary: List workspaces in the active organization
get.description:
Paginated with the shared list dialect. Workspaces are the unit devices belong to, so this is usually the second call a client makes after `GET /me`.

A workspace-scoped session token lists exactly one workspace: its own. Any other reads as `404` from `GET /workspaces/{id}`, indistinguishable from a workspace in another organization.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Sort column. Anything else is a 400.

post.summary: Create a workspace in the active organization
post.description:
Open to role `member`, which is what makes programmatic customer onboarding work: a consumer running its own multi-tenancy creates one workspace per customer with its default-role API key.

Workspace WRITES are organization-wide, so a workspace-scoped session token is refused with `403 WORKSPACE_SCOPED` whatever role it carries. Creating and deleting tenants is your backend's job, done with the key; a browser-held credential that could delete its own tenant would be a liability with no matching use.

get.summary: Get a workspace

put.description: Partial update. An empty body is a 400. Organization-wide, like every workspace write: a workspace-scoped session token gets `403 WORKSPACE_SCOPED`.

delete.description: Deletes every device in the workspace the way `DELETE /devices/{id}` does — IoT identity, video channels, uploaded media and telemetry included — then the workspace, its logo, and any session token scoped to it. There is no undo. Organization-wide: a workspace-scoped session token gets `403 WORKSPACE_SCOPED`.

put.description: Identical in every respect to `PUT /organizations/{id}/logo` — base64 body, declared type checked against the bytes, private object, presigned `logoUrl` on the response — one level down. Organization-wide, like every workspace write: a workspace-scoped session token gets `403 WORKSPACE_SCOPED`.

contentType.description: Must match what the bytes actually are.

data.description: Base64 with no `data:` prefix. Decodes to at most 1.5 MB; larger is a 400.

delete.description: Clears the logo; clients fall back to the initials of the name. Idempotent — a workspace with no logo answers 200 with `logoUrl: null`.

get.summary: List the platform-wide device model catalog
get.description: The catalog is PLATFORM-wide, not per organization, so this endpoint takes no tenancy header and every authenticated caller sees the same rows. Paginated with the shared list dialect. Writes need the platform-admin role (`users.role = "admin"`), which is separate from any membership role. The envelope keys are `device_models` / `device_model` (snake_case, mirroring the table name) with camelCase contents; the SDKs present them as `deviceModels` / `deviceModel`.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Sort column. Anything else is a 400.

post.summary: Add a device model (platform admin only)
post.description: `ioCapabilities` is what makes a model useful: it declares the video/audio stream keys that become video channels at provisioning time, and the telemetry metrics that become the default history columns. It is NOT validated here, but it IS parsed at provisioning time, and a document that fails that parse provisions zero video channels. Check it against the schema before you send it.

get.summary: Get a device model

put.summary: Update a device model (platform admin only)
put.description: Partial update; an empty body is a 400. Changing `ioCapabilities` does not retro-provision video channels on devices already created from this model.

delete.summary: Delete a device model (platform admin only)

get.summary: List devices in the active organization
get.description: Every device whose workspace belongs to the active organization, paginated with the shared list dialect. Pass `X-Workspace-Id` to narrow it to one workspace; a workspace outside the active organization returns an EMPTY page rather than an error, so an empty result never distinguishes "no devices" from "wrong workspace".

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Sort column. Anything else is a 400.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Filter by device status. An empty value or the literal `any` means "no filter"; any other unknown value is a 400.

parameters.name: simulated
parameters.description: `true` lists only simulated devices (see Device Simulations), `false` only real ones. Absent lists both. Any other value is a 400.

post.summary: Register a device under a workspace in the active organization
post.description: Creates the row only. It has no IoT identity until `POST /devices/{id}/provision`, and no agent until someone installs one. For onboarding a physical device, prefer the registration-code flow, which does all three in one pass.

workspaceId.description: Must belong to the active organization, else 400.

get.summary: Get a device

put.description: Metadata only. `status` and `lastSeenAt` are machine-managed (telemetry ingest, the MQTT last-will, and the offline sweeper own them) and are rejected 400. `deviceModelId` reassigns the device model (resolving a `needsModel` device, or correcting a wrong model): it clears `needsModel` and republishes the device config with a bumped rev so the new model's hardware block reaches the device — it does NOT re-mint KVS channels. Device config moved to PATCH /devices/{id}/config and PATCH /devices/{id}/ui-prefs; the old per-namespace body fields below are still accepted for the transition window, forwarded through the same validation into `config`/`uiPrefs`, and logged as deprecated.

deviceModelId.description: Reassign the device model. Clears `needsModel` and delivers the new model's hardware block via a rev-bumped config republish.

502.description: A legacy config field was accepted and saved, but publishing the retained document to the device failed (`CONFIG_PUBLISH_FAILED`).

delete.description: Removes the device and everything it owns: the row and what cascades off it (identity, video channels, sessions, workflow attachments and runs), its telemetry history, AND the AWS side — the IoT thing and certificate, the KVS signaling channels, and the uploaded media and telemetry objects. The AWS teardown is best-effort: a device with a very large upload history may leave objects behind, which the bucket lifecycle expires (recorded media within 90 days). There is no undo. The device agent, if still running, loses its identity and must be re-enrolled with a new claim code.

patch.description: Writes one or more namespaces of the device config document, bumps `configRev`, and publishes the whole document as a retained MQTT message on `xorgate/devices/{id}/config`. Each present namespace is validated and replaced WHOLE, because the device replaces namespaces the same way and a partial namespace would silently drop the keys it omits. `null` reverts a namespace to device defaults. Two namespaces are gated on the device: `simulation` is accepted only for a simulated device and `obd` only for a device whose model declares `peripherals.obd` (400 otherwise, naming the namespace). Returns 502 when the row was written but the retained publish failed: the device has NOT been told yet, though it self-heals on its next config report.

schema.description: Partial config document. Present namespaces are validated and replaced WHOLE (matching how the device merges); `null` reverts a namespace to device defaults on BOTH sides, so the cloud stops managing it and the device is told to drop its local value; absent namespaces are untouched; `{}` is rejected. All-or-nothing: any invalid namespace fails the whole request, so a multi-namespace save can never half-commit.

gnssAntBias.description: GPS antenna bias (`gnssAntBias`): true powers an active antenna over the coax, false (default) is the passive/bias-off hardware-safe state. Apply class: `modem-poll`. null reverts to device defaults.

imuMount.description: IMU mounting correction (`imuMount` namespace): how the sensor is physically rotated relative to the vehicle (ZYX euler, degrees). All four fields are required. Applied live by the IMU collector; absent = no correction. Apply class: `agent-poll`. null reverts to device defaults.

recording.description: On-device recording settings (`recording` namespace). All fields optional — omitted fields fall back to device defaults. Unknown keys and out-of-range values are rejected. Applied live by the agent (5 s settings poll, and forced on every cloud config message); toggling video recording or changing its preset briefly restarts the live stream. Apply class: `agent-poll`. null reverts to device defaults.

lteRecovery.description: LTE recovery policy (`lteRecovery` namespace): how aggressively the device connection manager may use the GNSS-destructive full modem reset. Both fields optional; omitted fields fall back to the device defaults. Read live by the modem daemon at its next recovery decision — no device restart. Apply class: `modem-poll`. null reverts to device defaults.

timeSync.description: Offline time sources (`timeSync` namespace): while NTP is unsynced this boot, the agent may step the system clock from GPS (valid GNSS fix) or the modem NITZ clock, then stand down for the boot once NTP synchronizes. All fields optional; omitted fields fall back to the device defaults. Apply class: `agent-poll`. null reverts to device defaults.

cellular.description: Cellular data-context settings (`cellular` namespace). `apn` empty or absent leaves the modem's stored APN untouched (the safe default). A non-empty APN is applied by the modem daemon with apply-and-confirm rollback: real traffic must flow over the modem interface within a bounded window or the previous APN is restored automatically. Read live from settings.json by the modem daemon — never restart it to apply a setting. Apply class: `modem-poll`. null reverts to device defaults.

cameraMount.description: Camera mounting rotation (`cameraMount` namespace): per-camera 0/180 applied at the image sensor via the camera overlay in /boot/firmware/config.txt, so live video, recordings, replays and workflow frames are all corrected at zero CPU cost. ⚠️ Applies on the NEXT BOOT: the agent edits the boot config and reports the namespace with a `rebootRequired` detail; it never reboots the device itself. An absent camera key is unmanaged (the boot config is left as found); an explicit `rotationDeg: 0` forces that camera upright. Apply class: `agent-poll`. null reverts to device defaults.

simulation.description: Device-simulator scenario selection (`simulation` namespace). Accepted only for devices created as simulated; a simulated device replays the catalog scenario `scenarioId` from `demo-assets/v1/`, parks for `gapSeconds` between laps, and loops while `loop` is true. Applied live by the replay source (5 s settings poll, and forced on every cloud config message); a changed scenarioId ends the current lap in place. Apply class: `agent-poll`. null reverts to device defaults.

obd.description: Vehicle OBD-II adapter settings (`obd` namespace). Accepted only for devices whose model declares `peripherals.obd` (400 otherwise). Every field is optional and an omitted field falls back to the device default, but the namespace is replaced WHOLE on write (send the fields you want to keep). `adapterMac` names the ELM327 Bluetooth adapter the device pairs with (stored uppercase; the device never pairs by name), `enabled` is the polling kill switch, `fields` narrows the polled set below the model's declared list (empty = all), and `powerSource` says how the tracker device (not the adapter) is powered, which selects the battery policy. Applied live by the agent's OBD collector on its settings poll and on every cloud config message; a changed adapter restarts the helper. Pairing outcome, probe profile and scan candidates come back in the config report under `effective.obd`. Apply class: `agent-poll`. null reverts to device defaults.

cameraSensors.description: Camera sensor per port (`cameraSensors` namespace): which image sensor is attached to each camera port of this device, keyed by stream key. `sensor` is an id of the camera catalog or "none" for an empty port; `options` are that sensor's per-board overlay parameters. The agent makes the port's `dtoverlay=` line in /boot/firmware/config.txt match. ⚠️ Applies on the NEXT BOOT: the agent edits the boot config and reports that a reboot is required; it never reboots the device itself. An absent port key is unmanaged (the line is left as found). Accepted only for a real (not simulated) device running the Rust agent that either has not reported yet or advertises the `camera.sensors` capability; otherwise a 400 naming the agent version needed. Replaced WHOLE on write, so send every port you want to keep managed. Apply class: `agent-poll`. null reverts to device defaults.

502.description: Saved, but delivering it to the device failed (`CONFIG_PUBLISH_FAILED`). It will be delivered automatically the next time the device reports in.

patch.description: Cloud-only: nothing here is delivered to the device, nothing is published, and `configRev` is not bumped. `null` resets a pref to its default.

schema.description: Partial ui-prefs document. `null` resets a pref to its default. Cloud-only: nothing here is delivered to the device, and `configRev` is not bumped.

activeStreamsViewType.description: Layout for the Active Streams tab: card grid (default) or location-first map view.

azimuthDeg.description: Camera azimuth for the 3D orientation view, degrees.

elevationDeg.description: Camera elevation for the 3D orientation view, degrees. Bounded to ±85: at the poles the look-at up-vector degenerates and the view flips.

post.description: Mints an AWS IoT thing + X.509 certificate, attaches the device policy, and creates a video channel per declared video stream. Returns the certificate, private key, and connection endpoints exactly once, so persist them on the device immediately. A second call for an already-provisioned device returns 409; certificate rotation is not supported yet.

201.description: Device provisioned. Credential bundle shown only here.

get.summary: The device's IoT identity metadata
get.description: Non-secret fields of the X.509 identity minted at provisioning time: thing name, certificate id, policy, role alias, status. `identity` is NULL (with a 200, not a 404) when the device exists but has not been provisioned, so a client can render a clean "not provisioned" state. Reads the database only; it does not call AWS IoT, so a certificate revoked out of band still reads `active` here.

200.description: Identity metadata, or null when the device is not provisioned.

post.summary: Move a device to another workspace
post.description:
Changes which workspace — and therefore which organization — owns a device.

**What moves.** Everything. The device record, its IoT identity and certificates, its video channels, ALL of its historical telemetry, and ALL of its recorded footage. Telemetry and media are stored against the device, not against a tenant, so they travel with it and nothing is purged. For a transfer between organizations that is a data-disclosure event; call the preview first and show the operator what it says.

**What does not move.** Workflow attachments pointing at the source organization's templates are DETACHED (the destination cannot see those templates), and the names are returned in `transfer.detachedWorkflowAttachments`. Workflow runs already executing are left to finish. Session tokens scoped to the source workspace stop seeing the device and are not revoked. Completed run history, dataset items and the registration record stay where they are — they are history of the device under its former owner.

**The device does not have to be online.** Nothing on the device changes: certificates and identity are untouched and the tenancy is never stored on the box. An offline device has its new tenancy staged in the cloud and adopts it the moment it next connects — no reboot, no re-provisioning, no site visit. That is a normal success, reported through `transfer.warnings`, not an error.

**Completion is two-step, and the response says which step it is at.** The ownership change is complete and authoritative the moment this returns 200. Whether the DEVICE has caught up is a separate question, answered by `transfer.adoption`: `pending` is the normal immediate answer, `confirmed` appears once the device reports publishing under the new tenancy, and `unknown` means it has never reported a telemetry scope (every agent older than v0.0.6). Poll `GET /devices/{id}` to watch it settle.

**Cross-organization.** Pass `organizationId` to move the device into another organization you personally administer (`owner` or `admin` in BOTH). Without that shared membership — a genuine handover to a customer — use a transfer offer instead: `POST /devices/{id}/transfer-offers`. API keys cannot use the shared-membership path at all, because a key is bound to one organization by its own record.

**Operational precondition.** A device whose agent predates `v0.0.6` has no fallback to the unscoped telemetry topic, so a transfer that it cannot immediately act on can leave it unable to publish until its agent process is restarted. Update the fleet before transferring fielded devices.

organizationId.description: The DESTINATION organization. Only needed when it differs from the active one, and only usable by a user holding `owner` or `admin` in it.

200.description: Transferred. Includes the case where the device is offline and will converge on its next connect — read `transfer.warnings` and `transfer.adoption`.

400.description: Malformed body, an unknown field, or a destination equal to the device's current workspace (`SAME_WORKSPACE`).

403.description: The caller is a `member` or `viewer`, holds a workspace-scoped session token (a transfer spans two workspaces, so such a credential can never be authorized for both), or is an API key attempting the shared-membership cross-organization path.

404.description: The device was not found, or the destination workspace is not one the caller can reach. Deliberately indistinguishable: confirming that another tenant's workspace exists would itself be a leak.

409.description: A device with the same serial already exists in the destination workspace (`SERIAL_COLLISION` — serials are unique per workspace), or another transfer of this device is already running (`TRANSFER_IN_PROGRESS`), or the device moved while the request was being prepared (`CONCURRENT_MODIFICATION`).

502.description: The device could not be told about its new workspace, so the transfer was ROLLED BACK and nothing changed (`TRANSFER_FAILED`). Safe to retry.

get.summary: What a transfer would do, without doing it
get.description:
A dry run of `POST /devices/{id}/transfer`. Writes nothing.

It exists so a confirmation can NAME the consequences before the operator agrees rather than report them afterwards — in particular the workflow attachments a cross-organization move will detach, which cannot be reconsidered once the transfer has run.

Refusals come back in `blockers` rather than as an error status, so the reason can be shown in place. `POST` turns the first blocker into its own 400 or 409.

parameters.name: workspaceId
parameters.description: The DESTINATION workspace.

parameters.name: organizationId
parameters.description: The DESTINATION organization, for the shared-membership cross-organization path. Same authorization as on `POST`.

get.summary: List purges of a device (owner/admin only)
get.description: The purge history of a device, newest first: the audit record of who wiped what and when, and the way a client finds a purge that is still running. At most 20.

post.description:
Deletes the history a device has accumulated while keeping the device itself: its row, identity and certificate, live video channels, settings, webhook routes and the latest-value cache all stay, and the agent keeps running. What goes is chosen per `scope`:

- `workflows`: every workflow attached to the device is detached, and every production run those attachments produced (and the runs of workflows detached earlier) is deleted with its steps, events and S3 artifacts. Runs still executing are stopped. The organization's workflow templates and their simulation runs are untouched.
- `telemetry`: recorded telemetry sessions, their segments, overview artifacts, ingest log and every stored reading.
- `media`: recorded video sessions, their segments and thumbnails.

Everything older than the moment of the request (`cutoff`) is removed; what the device uploads afterwards stays. A recording in progress is cut at that point. The work runs asynchronously: this returns `202` with the purge row, and `GET /devices/{id}/purges/{purgeId}` reports progress until `status` is `succeeded` or `failed`. One purge per device at a time. There is no undo.

Organization-wide: a workspace-scoped session token is refused (`WORKSPACE_SCOPED`).

202.description: Purge queued. Poll `GET /devices/{id}/purges/{purgeId}` for the outcome.

409.description: A purge of this device is already queued or running (`PURGE_IN_PROGRESS`; `details.purgeId` names it), or a cross-organization transfer offer for the device is pending (`TRANSFER_PENDING`).

502.description: The purge was recorded but could not be queued (`PURGE_DISPATCH_FAILED`). Nothing was deleted; the row is marked `failed`. Safe to retry.

get.summary: What a purge would remove, without removing it
get.description: Counts per scope for the confirmation step of `POST /devices/{id}/purges`. Writes nothing. Stored readings are reported as a time span rather than a count: counting them is the expensive part of the purge itself.

200.description: What a purge of each scope would remove, as of now.

get.summary: Get a purge (owner/admin only)
get.description: One purge: its status, what it has removed so far (`counts`) and where it is (`cursor.step`). Poll every few seconds while `status` is `queued` or `running`.

post.summary: Read the SMS stored on a device's SIM and modem
post.description:
Asks the device to read the text messages its cellular modem holds (SIM and modem storage) and return the newest `limit`. Reading is non-destructive: nothing is deleted and unread messages stay unread. Returns `202` with a `pending` read; poll `GET /devices/{id}/sms-reads/{readId}` (every second or two) until `status` is no longer `pending`. A read takes a few seconds and expires after 45 s.

Xorgate keeps only the device's latest successful read (served by `GET /devices/{id}/sms-reads/latest`, also while the device is offline); each new successful read replaces it. Any member of the organization may read, viewers included.

202.description: Read requested. Poll it by id.

400.description: `limit` is not a number, or the body is not a JSON object (`VALIDATION_ERROR`).

409.description: The device is not online (`DEVICE_OFFLINE`), or its agent predates SMS reading (`UNSUPPORTED_AGENT`; update the device agent).

502.description: The command could not be delivered to the broker (`COMMAND_PUBLISH_FAILED`; `details.readId` names the read, now `error`). Safe to retry.

get.summary: The device's stored messages (its latest successful read)
get.description: The newest read whose `status` is `ok`, with its messages. Works whatever the device's status, which is the point: an offline device still shows what was last fetched. A successful clear (`action: "clear"`) counts too, so after one this serves its (normally empty) result until the next read. 404 `NO_SMS_READ` when the device has never been read.

404.description: No such device (`NOT_FOUND`), or it has never been read (`NO_SMS_READ`).

get.summary: Get an SMS read
get.description: One read: `pending` while the device works, then `ok` (with `result`) or `error`. A read still `pending` 45 s after it was requested is returned, and stored, as `expired` (`errorCode: "timeout"`). Unknown ids, ids of another device and non-uuid ids are 404.

post.summary: Delete every SMS stored on a device's SIM and modem (owner/admin only)
post.description:
Asks the device to delete every text message its cellular modem holds (SIM and modem storage), then read the stores again. A full store makes the modem refuse new messages; this empties it. **Destructive and irreversible**, so only owners and admins may clear (members and viewers get `403` `INSUFFICIENT_ROLE`).

Returns `202` with a `pending` `SmsRead` whose `action` is `clear`; poll `GET /devices/{id}/sms-reads/{readId}` exactly as for a read. On `ok`, `result` is the device's state after the delete (normally no messages, with fresh storage counts) plus `cleared`, how many messages each store held before. A successful clear replaces the stored copy, so `GET /devices/{id}/sms-reads/latest` serves it until the next read and the previously stored message text is gone from Xorgate too. `limit` sizes that follow-up read, with the same rules as a read.

202.description: Clear requested. Poll it by id.

400.description: `limit` is not a number, or the body is not a JSON object (`VALIDATION_ERROR`).

403.description: Not an owner or admin of the organization (`INSUFFICIENT_ROLE`), or not a member.

409.description: The device is not online (`DEVICE_OFFLINE`), or its agent predates clearing (`UNSUPPORTED_AGENT`; update the device agent).

502.description: The command could not be delivered to the broker (`COMMAND_PUBLISH_FAILED`; `details.readId` names the clear, now `error`). Nothing was deleted. Safe to retry.

post.description: Publishes a one-shot reboot command over MQTT and returns immediately. 202 means the command was delivered to the broker, not that the device has rebooted; observe the outcome via the device status, which goes offline and then back online. The device must be online (409 otherwise), because commands are not retained and there is nothing for an offline device to pick up later. The command expires 60 seconds after issue and carries a request id the device refuses to execute twice, so a stale or redelivered command cannot cause a surprise reboot.
Same delivery semantics and guards as reboot, but NOT remotely recoverable: the device stays off until someone physically powers it back on. The device must be online (409 otherwise).

post.summary: Ask the device to re-probe and re-report its state now
post.description: A one-shot READ-ONLY command: the device re-probes what it can (SIM identity, applied APN, antenna bias) and publishes a fresh config report immediately instead of on its hourly heartbeat. Observe the outcome by re-reading the device until `reportedAt` advances. The device rate-limits refreshes to roughly one per 30 s and a re-probe takes up to about 45 s to land. Ordinary member access, since nothing on the device changes. The device must be online (409 otherwise).

post.summary: Install the latest agent build on a device (owner/admin only)
post.description: Publishes a one-shot update command over MQTT. The device starts a systemd one-shot that downloads the latest published build (see GET /device-dist/latest), installs it, and restarts the agent, so the device drops offline for roughly a minute or two. Latest-only: there is no version parameter. A failed install rolls back, leaving the device on its current build. IMPORTANT: 202 means the command reached the broker, NOT that the update succeeded, and the ack could not tell you either (the agent is restarted mid-update). Observe the outcome by polling GET /devices/{id} until `agentVersion` changes; an unchanged build after the device returns online means the update failed and rolled back (diagnose on the device with `journalctl -u xorgate-updater`). The device must be online (409 otherwise). Pressing this twice is harmless: `systemctl start` on an already-running one-shot coalesces into the run in flight.

post.summary: Ask an OBD-II kit to scan for nearby Bluetooth adapters
post.description: Publishes a one-shot `obd_scan` command over MQTT. The device runs one bounded Bluetooth discovery (it never pairs with anything it finds) and writes the candidates into its next config report as `effective.obd.scan = { ts, candidates: [{ mac, name, rssi }] }`. Observe the outcome by re-reading `GET /devices/{id}` until `reportedConfig.effective.obd.scan.ts` advances past the request (typically 10 to 20 s); there is no result row to poll and the command ack is not consumed, because the answer travels on the reported config plane the device already maintains. The operator then picks a MAC and writes it with `PATCH /devices/{id}/config {"obd": {"adapterMac": "..."}}`. Only for a device whose model declares `peripherals.obd` (`400` `NOT_OBD_DEVICE` otherwise). Rate-limited server-side to one scan per device per 60 s (`429` `RATE_LIMITED`, `details.retryAfterMs`), because discovery stalls the helper's polling while it runs. Ordinary member access, since nothing on the device changes. The device must be online (409 otherwise).

400.description: The device's model does not declare `peripherals.obd` (`NOT_OBD_DEVICE`): it has no OBD reader to scan with.

429.description: A scan was requested for this device inside the last 60 s (`RATE_LIMITED`; `details.retryAfterMs` says how long to wait). Read the candidates it produced instead.

post.summary: Ask an OBD-II kit to forget its paired adapter
post.description: Publishes a one-shot `obd_forget` command over MQTT. The device drops the Bluetooth bond for its configured adapter and stops polling it; the next config report shows `effective.obd.status` back at "not configured". The cloud-side setting is NOT cleared by this call: pair it with `PATCH /devices/{id}/config {"obd": null}` (revert the whole namespace) or `{"obd": {"adapterMac": null, ...}}`, otherwise the retained config re-pairs the same adapter on the device's next settings poll. Reversible (set an adapter again), so it takes the ordinary write gate (owner/admin/member). Only for a device whose model declares `peripherals.obd` (`400` `NOT_OBD_DEVICE` otherwise). The device must be online (409 otherwise).

400.description: The device's model does not declare `peripherals.obd` (`NOT_OBD_DEVICE`).

parameters.name: agent
parameters.description: Select one agent's channel. WITH it the response is self-describing (`{agent, latest | null, registrationEnabled}`, always 200 for a readable or missing manifest). WITHOUT it the response is the historical `{latest}` for the JS agent, with 404 when unpublished. A backend that predates this parameter ignores it and answers in the historical shape, which carries no `agent`: read that as "this API does not support the Rust agent".

parameters.name: X-Workspace-Id
parameters.description: With `?agent=`: the workspace `registrationEnabled` is evaluated for. Without it, Rust registration counts as enabled only when the stage enables it everywhere.

get.summary: The newest published device-agent build
get.description: Returns the manifest the device-agent CI publishes alongside the `latest` tarball alias, which is exactly what a device update would install for this stage. Fleet-wide, not per-device. Compare `version` against a device's reported build (`agentVersion`) by STRING EQUALITY only: shas do not order, and a dev sha and a prod release tag are not comparable. 404 means CI has not published a manifest for this stage yet, which is "latest unknown" rather than an error. Pass `?agent=js|rust` for one agent's channel (the Rust agent has its own manifest); compare a device against the channel of its own `agent`.

200.description: The latest published build. Without `agent`: `{latest}` (the JS agent). With `agent`: `{agent, latest | null, registrationEnabled}`.

latest.description: null = no manifest is published for this agent on this stage.

registrationEnabled.description: Whether `POST /device-registrations` accepts this agent here. Always true for `js`; for `rust`, the stage flag evaluated for `X-Workspace-Id`.

404.description: Without `agent` only: no manifest is published for this stage yet.

500.description: This stage has no distribution bucket configured (`DIST_BUCKET_UNCONFIGURED`).

502.description: The manifest object is unreadable, empty, oversized, or carries no version (`DIST_MANIFEST_UNAVAILABLE`, `DIST_MANIFEST_INVALID`).

post.description: Starts onboarding: returns a short-lived code and the `installUrl` to run on the device. `X-Workspace-Id` is REQUIRED here (unlike on `GET /devices`, where it is a filter), because the code carries the workspace the future device will land in. Idempotent per workspace: while a pending, un-expired code exists it is returned again instead of minting a new one, so reloading a dialog does not burn codes. The device model defaults to the most recently created one, and a deployment with no device models is a 400 — but the default is only a FALLBACK: the claim maps the device's own hardware probe to a model row (probe-at-claim), unless `deviceModelId` is passed here to pin the model explicitly (the claim then skips the probe). Passing `deviceModelId` while a pending code exists re-pins that code's model in place. `agent` picks the installer the code serves (`js`, the default, or `rust`); a pending code is reused only for the SAME agent, so changing the agent mints a new code. `rust` is gated per stage, and optionally per workspace: while it is not enabled the request is a 409 `AGENT_NOT_ENABLED`. `cameras` (Rust registrations only) carries the camera sensor chosen per port; like the model pick it is re-pinned in place on a pending code. Note the success status is 200, not 201, even when a code is created.

deviceModelId.description: Pin the device model explicitly instead of probe-at-claim mapping. Unknown ids are a 400.

agent.description: Which device agent the installer installs. Absent = `js`. Any other value is a 400 `INVALID_AGENT`; `rust` while this stage does not enable it for the workspace is a 409 `AGENT_NOT_ENABLED` (see `GET /device-dist/latest?agent=rust` `registrationEnabled`).

cameras.description: Rust registrations only (`agent: "rust"`): the camera sensor on each port, which the claim stores as the new device's `cameraSensors` config namespace. A port left out starts on the device model's own sensor. Absent = leave a reused pending code's choice as it is; `null` or `{}` = clear it. Passing it while a pending code exists re-pins that code's choice in place. On a JS registration, and for a sensor or option the camera catalog does not list, it is a 400 `INVALID_CAMERAS`. A key the model resolved at claim does not declare is dropped at claim. The choice is applied only when the installer that claims the code declares the `camera.sensors` capability (Rust agent 0.2.0 or newer); an older installer leaves the device on its model's sensors, unmanaged.

200.description: A pending registration, freshly minted or the existing un-expired one.

400.description: Bad request, including an unknown `agent` (`INVALID_AGENT`) or `deviceModelId`, and a `cameras` value that is not valid or not allowed (`INVALID_CAMERAS`).

409.description: `agent: "rust"` while Rust-agent registration is not enabled on this stage for this workspace (`AGENT_NOT_ENABLED`).

get.summary: Poll a registration code
get.description: How a client watches onboarding finish: poll until `status` is `claimed` and `deviceId` is set. Reading also lazily expires a stale pending row, so the `expired` status appears on read rather than on a schedule. Scoped to the active organization, so another organization's code is a 404.

post.summary: Claim a registration code (internal, installer only)
post.description: INTERNAL. Called unauthenticated by the install script running on the device. It flips the code to `claimed`, creates the device row, provisions its AWS IoT identity, and returns the certificate and PRIVATE KEY once. The body may carry a hardware probe (`dtModel` = /proc/device-tree/model, `cameras` = libcamera count, 0 = unknown) that picks the device model unless the registration pinned one; an ambiguous probe keeps the registration's model and flags the device `needsModel`. The response embeds the resolved model's device-facing `hardware` block (null for schemaVersion-1 models), which the installer writes to /etc/xorgate/hardware.json. The body may also carry `capabilities`, a list of capability strings the installer and the agent it installs can act on (at most 32 items of at most 64 characters; anything else, and any string the backend does not know, is ignored and is never an error). For a Rust registration whose claim lists `camera.sensors`, the claim seeds the device's `cameraSensors` config namespace (per camera port of the resolved model: the registration's `cameras` choice, else the model's sensor) and returns it as `cameraSensors`. Without that string nothing is seeded or returned and the registration's `cameras` choice is not applied; a JS claim never stores or returns anything new. When the probe reports 0 cameras, the number of sensors the registration declares stands in as the count. Not part of the public API surface: treat the installer as the only client.

200.description: Device created and provisioned. Response withheld from public docs.

get.summary: Device install script (internal, installer only)
get.description: INTERNAL. Serves the bash installer for a registration code as `text/x-shellscript`, unauthenticated. The registration's `agent` picks it: `js` gets the JS agent installer, `rust` a bootstrap that downloads, verifies and runs the Rust agent's own provisioner. Invalid, used, or expired codes still return a runnable script that prints the reason and exits non-zero, so the operator sees the problem instead of bash silently doing nothing.

400.description: Missing code. Body is a failing shell script.

404.description: Unknown code. Body is a failing shell script.

409.description: A `rust` code while Rust-agent registration is not enabled here. Body is a failing shell script.

410.description: Code already used or expired. Body is a failing shell script.

500.description: Server misconfiguration. Body is a failing shell script.

post.description: Creates a device that is the real device agent replaying a recorded drive in a container on a simulator host: online within a couple of minutes, live video, moving on the map, five seeded recorded sessions, and no hardware. In order: a quota check (`409 SIMULATION_QUOTA_EXCEEDED`; 2 per organization and 8 overall by default), a device row (serial `SIM-<8 hex>`, model Argus CM5 Rev1, `simulated: true`, cam1 disabled, the `simulation` namespace set), the same IoT thing, certificate and video channels a real device gets, the first config publish, and the credentials handed to the host. Any failure after the row exists is rolled back and is a `502 SIMULATION_PROVISION_FAILED`. From then on it is a normal device: configure, command, browse and DELETE it through `/devices/{id}`. To switch scenario, PATCH the device's `simulation` namespace (whole) and send `POST /devices/{id}/reboot`.

workspaceId.description: Must belong to the active organization, else 400.

scenarioId.description: A scenario from `GET /device-simulations/scenarios`; an id the catalog does not carry is a 400. Defaults to the catalog default.

201.description: The simulated device and its simulation. The host picks it up within one pass.

502.description: Provisioning failed and was rolled back (`SIMULATION_PROVISION_FAILED`). Retry.

get.summary: List the scenarios a simulated device can replay
get.description: The scenario catalog of the current asset pack: recorded drives a simulated device replays on a loop. Thumbnail URLs are presigned and expire after an hour.

defaultScenarioId.description: What `POST /device-simulations` uses when no `scenarioId` is sent.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The simulated DEVICE id. A simulation is 1:1 with its device and has no id of its own.

get.summary: Read a simulated device's simulation state
get.description: What the host has been asked to do (`desiredState`, `startRequestedAt`) and what it last reported (`hostState`, `hostMessage`, `hostReportedAt`). A device that is not simulated is a 404.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The simulated DEVICE id. A simulation is 1:1 with its device and has no id of its own.

post.description: The power button a powered-off simulated device lacks. A `power_off` command parks the sim and it stays off (the host reports `hostState: stopped`); this sets `desiredState: running` and stamps `startRequestedAt`, and the host powers the sim on at its next pass. Idempotent; on a running sim it changes nothing the device notices.

post.summary: Offer a device to another organization
post.description:
Mints a code that another organization can redeem to take ownership of this device.

Use this when you do NOT share a membership with the destination — a genuine handover to a customer. If you personally hold `owner` or `admin` in both organizations, `POST /devices/{id}/transfer` with an `organizationId` does the same move in one call.

**The code is a bearer token.** Anyone holding it can read the offer's preview and accept or decline it. Send it over a channel you trust. It expires after 7 days.

**Idempotent.** A device has at most one open offer. Calling this again while one is pending returns the existing offer with **200** instead of minting a second claimable code; a genuinely new offer returns **201**.

`willDetachWorkflowAttachments` names the workflow templates this device is attached to. If the offer is accepted by a different organization they are all detached, because they belong to yours and the new owner cannot see them. It is returned HERE, at creation, because you are not present when the offer is accepted — this is the last point at which you can reconsider.

200.description: An offer was already open for this device; it is returned unchanged.

get.summary: Every transfer offer ever made for a device
get.description: Open and resolved offers, newest first. A pending offer past its expiry is flipped to `expired` as it is read, so the status you see is always current.

get.summary: Transfer offers this organization sent or accepted
get.description:
Offers your organization CREATED, plus offers it has already ACCEPTED, newest first. `direction` tells them apart.

**There is no inbox of incoming pending offers, by design.** An offer names no destination — that is exactly what lets it be handed to an organization whose id the sender does not know — so a pending offer is discoverable only by its code. If someone has offered you a device, you will have been sent a code; read it with `GET /transfer-offers/{code}`.

Declines are visible here: an offer the destination refused reads `declined` with `resolvedAt` set, rather than quietly expiring.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Filter by status. Anything else is a 400.

parameters.name: code
parameters.description: The offer code. Treat it as a secret: it is what authorizes the destination to read the offer and act on it.

get.summary: Read an offer you were sent a code for
get.description:
What the code buys, and nothing else: the device's name and model, the offering organization's name, and the offer's own status and expiry.

**Deliberately absent**: the device id, its serial, its workspace, its configuration and its telemetry. Whoever holds the code is not yet entitled to the device, so the code must not double as a read primitive against someone else's fleet.

Any role may read this. Accepting or declining needs `owner` or `admin`.

delete.description: Only the organization that created the offer can cancel it, and only while it is still pending. An offer belonging to another organization reads as **404**, not 403.

204.description: Cancelled. The code no longer works.

409.description: The offer has already been accepted, declined, cancelled or expired.

parameters.name: code
parameters.description: The offer code. Treat it as a secret: it is what authorizes the destination to read the offer and act on it.

post.summary: Take ownership of an offered device
post.description:
Moves the device into one of YOUR workspaces and runs the full transfer, including the cross-organization sweep. Requires `owner` or `admin` in the accepting organization.

Everything in `POST /devices/{id}/transfer` applies from here on: all historical telemetry and all recorded footage come with the device, the device does not have to be online, and `transfer.adoption` says whether it has confirmed the change yet.

Accepting is race-safe: the offer is claimed with a conditional write before the transfer runs, so only one of two simultaneous accepts wins. If the transfer itself fails the offer is put back to `pending` and the code can be retried.

workspaceId.description: The workspace in YOUR organization the device should land in.

400.description: Malformed body, or the offer was created by your own organization (use `POST /devices/{id}/transfer` instead).

404.description: No such offer, or the named workspace is not one of yours. Deliberately indistinguishable.

409.description: The offer is already resolved or expired, the device is mid-transfer, a device with the same serial already exists in the destination workspace, or the offering organization no longer owns the device (the offer is stale).

502.description: The device could not be told about its new workspace. The transfer was rolled back and the offer is still open.

parameters.name: code
parameters.description: The offer code. Treat it as a secret: it is what authorizes the destination to read the offer and act on it.

post.description: Marks the offer `declined` and closes it. The sender sees the decline in `GET /transfer-offers`, so a refusal is an answer rather than an offer that quietly expires. Requires `owner` or `admin`.

409.description: The offer is already resolved or expired.

get.summary: Query historical telemetry over a time range
get.description:
Stored readings for the device over `[from, to)`, ordered by `ts` then `metric`. Both bounds are REQUIRED and the range may not exceed 31 days.

With `interval` (seconds) the result is downsampled server-side: readings are grouped into `interval`-wide buckets per metric and averaged, up to 10,000 buckets. Without it, raw rows are returned up to 5,000. Either way `truncated: true` means the cap was hit and the result is incomplete, so narrow the range or pass a coarser `interval`. This endpoint does not paginate; `truncated` is the only signal that data was left behind.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Range start (inclusive), ISO-8601.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Range end (exclusive), ISO-8601.

parameters.name: metric
parameters.description: Comma-separated metric filter, at most 20 names. Each must look like `group.field`; anything else is a 400.

parameters.name: interval
parameters.description: Downsample bucket width in seconds. An interval that would produce more than 5,000 buckets for the requested range is a 400.

200.description: Telemetry readings (raw or bucket-averaged), ordered by ts then metric.

bucketSeconds.description: Echo of `interval`; null when raw rows were returned.

truncated.description: True when the row cap was hit and the result is incomplete.

get.summary: The device's most recent reading per metric
get.description: One row per metric, last-writer-wins, ordered by metric. This is the cheap "what is the device doing right now" read and the authoritative source of a metric's unit. Empty when the device has never reported telemetry. It reflects the last reading INGESTED, so on an offline device it keeps returning stale values rather than nothing; check the timestamps.

get.summary: The newest N readings, with no time window
get.description: The newest `limit` rows for the device, returned in chronological order. Unlike `/telemetry` it takes no time window, so it never comes back empty just because the device last reported weeks ago. That makes it the right call for seeding a chart on page load, with the live MQTT feed appending after it. The response shape is the same as `/telemetry`: `bucketSeconds` is always null (nothing is averaged), and `truncated` means the row limit was reached.

parameters.name: metric
parameters.description: Comma-separated metric filter, at most 20 names. Each must look like `group.field`; anything else is a 400.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Rows (not samples) to return. Out-of-range values are a 400 here, not clamped.

get.summary: One page of the telemetry history table
get.description:
Raw (un-averaged) stored samples for one page, paginated over DISTINCT timestamps so a page boundary never splits a sample. Defaults to the latest samples (`order=desc`) with no time window. `limit`/`offset` count timestamps (samples), not rows, and unlike the other list endpoints an out-of-range `limit` is a 400 rather than being clamped.

**Two response shapes, selected by `shape`.** `shape=table` (the DEFAULT) returns the table being displayed: an ordered `columns` list with stable units, and one `rows` entry per timestamp whose `v` array is positional against `columns`. `shape=flat` returns the original `readings: [{ts, metric, value, unit}]` rows, the same raw-rows contract as `/telemetry` and `/telemetry/recent`. The table shape is roughly 10x smaller on the wire (this API does not compress) and its column set does not vary with the page contents.

`page.total` is the distinct-timestamp count, **bounded at 10,000**: when more samples match, `page.totalIsCapped` is `true` and only the first 10,000 in the requested `order` are addressable (newest first by default). `page.coveredFrom`/`coveredTo` give the ISO span of that addressable slice. Narrow `from`/`to` to reach beyond it; an `offset` past the cap returns an empty page, not an error.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Timestamps (samples) per page.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Timestamps to skip (page offset).

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: Sort direction by ts.

parameters.name: metric
parameters.description: Comma-separated metric filter, at most 20 names, each `group.field`. Under `shape=table` this also fixes the column set (the columns and the filter are one value). Omit it and the columns are derived from the device model's capabilities.

parameters.name: shape
parameters.description: Response shape. `table` (default) returns `columns` + positional `rows`; `flat` returns the raw `readings` rows.

200.description: One page of the history table (`shape=table`), or of raw readings ordered by ts then metric (`shape=flat`).

columnSource.description: Where the column set came from. `request` is your `metric` filter. `model` is the device model's io_capabilities. `data` means the model declares nothing usable, so columns were discovered from this page's rows and may vary between pages. `data` with an empty `columns` means the model declares nothing AND this page has no data.

get.summary: Distance and moving time inside a window
get.description: What the device drove INSIDE `[from, to)`, integrated over the overview artifacts of the telemetry sessions overlapping the window with the same rules as each session's own `insights.distance` (accepted fixes, the 60 m/s jump reject, the 30 s gap break, the `gps.speed` stationary rule). Use it to roll up a media run, a day or a month: the per-session `insights` on the sessions listing describe WHOLE sessions, and telemetry sessions do not line up with video sessions (the recorder starts at boot, the camera after its GPS gate), so summing whole sessions that merely overlap a run over-counts. The grid is bucketed, so the number is within about a percent of the raw-sample insight (`method: "overview-haversine"`). A session whose overview is not built yet (open, or closed within the last minute) is listed with `source: "unbuilt"` and no numbers, and `partial` is true. One object read per overlapping built session; the window may span at most 31 days. For a device whose model declares `peripherals.obd`, each session and the total also carry `vehicle` (engine-on, idle, live-link time, fuel used, odometer delta, rpm and coolant maxima, refuel and DTC counts) from the same overview, clipped to the window.

post.summary: Distance and moving time inside many windows
post.description: The batch form of `GET /devices/{id}/telemetry/insights`: one windowed roll-up per entry of `windows`, returned in the same order and computed by exactly the same rules. Use it to roll up a page of media runs in one request instead of one request per run: the device's telemetry sessions are listed once for the whole batch, and each overview artifact is read once however many windows overlap it. At most 100 windows per request; each window is validated like the single read (`to` after `from`, at most 31 days), and the first invalid one answers `400` naming its index. POST only because the windows ride in the body; the route reads, it creates nothing.

200.description: One roll-up per window, in request order.

get.summary: List recorded telemetry sessions with their insights
get.description:
The index of what the device RECORDED, one row per telemetry session, with the counters and the `insights` block computed when its overview was built (distance, duration, max speed, stops, GPS quality, ...). This is the read for a sessions table or a roll-up such as "kilometres this month": it never opens an artifact and never touches object storage. No URLs; to play a session's telemetry, ask the replay manifest for its window.

A telemetry session is NOT a video session: both ids are minted independently on the device, so relate them by time. `from`/`to` match sessions OVERLAPPING the range, exactly like `GET /devices/{id}/sessions`, so a recording run's distance is the sum over the telemetry sessions returned for the run's window. `insights` is `null` on a session whose overview has not been built yet (it is `open`, or closed within the last minute or so). Listing has the same side effect as the media list: it closes stale sessions as it goes.

Paginated: `page.total` is exact. Sorted by session start, newest first by default.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Sessions per page. Out of range is a 400.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Filter by lifecycle state. Omit or pass `any` for both.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Sessions still recording at or after this instant (overlap semantics).

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Sessions that started before this instant (overlap semantics).

get.summary: List device-recorded media sessions
get.description:
Sessions recorded on the device itself and uploaded segment by segment to S3. Paginated with the shared list dialect, plus `streamKey` and `group`. The time filter matches sessions OVERLAPPING `[from, to)`, not just those started inside it, because a session spans a window. Each row carries computed rollups (`segmentCount`, `totalBytes`, `totalDurationMs`).

Pass `group=runs` to paginate RECORDING RUNS instead of sessions: one drive with N cameras is N sessions, and a run is the set of sessions whose intervals are within 60 s of each other. Under `group=runs` the response returns `runs` instead of `sessions` (with members nested), `page.total` counts runs, and every filter selects which RUNS to return rather than which sessions to cluster. So `streamKey=cam0` returns the runs cam0 recorded in with all of their cameras present, and a from/to range returns overlapping runs whole rather than clipped.

Listing also closes stale sessions as a side effect, which is why a session can flip from `open` to `closed` between two reads with nothing else having happened.

parameters.name: group
parameters.description: Group and paginate by recording run. Requires `sort=startedAt` (a run has no createdAt), and any other value is a 400.

parameters.name: streamKey
parameters.description: Filter to one camera.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: An empty value or the literal `any` means "no filter".

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: `startedAt` is when the device recorded; `createdAt` is when the row landed.

200.description: Sessions with per-session rollups, newest first by default, or with `group=runs` the recording runs with their member sessions nested. `page.total` counts whichever noun was returned.

delete.description: Deletes every segment object (video plus sidecar) from storage and removes the session and its segment index rows. Owner/admin only, because device-recorded sessions are not re-creatable. A segment still uploading from the device after the delete recreates the session index (ingest is at-least-once); delete again once the device has drained.

409.description: Storage is not configured for this stage (`CONFLICT`).

get.summary: List a session's full segment index
get.description: The whole ordered index in one response (`seq` ascending is chronological by construction). This is the replay and stitching input, so it is deliberately unpaginated: a session is bounded at a few hours of 60 s segments. It returns the index only; use the playback route or the replay manifest to get URLs you can fetch.

get.summary: Get a presigned playback URL for one segment
get.description: One segment at a time. For playing a span of media, the replay manifest batch-presigns everything in one call instead.

200.description: Presigned S3 GET URL for the segment MP4.

409.description: Storage is not configured for this stage (`CONFLICT`).

get.summary: Get a gap-aware replay manifest with presigned segment URLs
get.description:
One response feeds a whole replay: per-session timelines (effective durations and gaps, computed server-side so every client renders the same timeline) plus a presigned GET URL per segment. Address it by `sessionId` (single session) OR by `from`/`to` (every session overlapping the range, segments clipped to it, optional `streamKey` filter), never both. Caps: 600 segments in total, and in range mode 10 sessions and 24 hours. Exceeding a cap is a 400 telling you to narrow the request. Refetch before `urlExpiresAt` (epoch ms), which is the real URL TTL minus a 5-minute safety margin.

**Telemetry rides along.** `replay.telemetry` lists the recorded-telemetry sessions that overlap the replay window (in session mode, the merged video timeline; in range mode, `from`..`to`), each with a presigned `overview.v1` artifact and its raw segments clipped to the window, plus the session's `insights`. Nothing in it touches a database or a Lambda on fetch: the browser GETs the objects straight from storage, and the URLs share `urlExpiresAt` with the video ones. An `open` session has `overview: null`; build it from its `segments` and poll the manifest about every 60 s until it closes. Telemetry has its own cap of 1,500 segments, honoured by truncation (`telemetry.truncated: true`), not by a 400. Pass `telemetry=0` to omit the block; a device that recorded nothing in the window returns `{ "sessions": [] }`.

parameters.name: sessionId
parameters.description: Single-session mode. Mutually exclusive with from/to.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Range mode start (with `to`). ISO-8601, like the telemetry endpoints.

parameters.name: streamKey
parameters.description: Range mode only: limit to one camera.

parameters.name: telemetry
parameters.description: `0` omits `replay.telemetry` (video-only clients, or a client that fetches telemetry by other means). Anything else, or absent, includes it.

200.description: The replay manifest. Timestamps are epoch ms.

get.summary: List the device's live video channels
get.description: Channel METADATA only, one entry per provisioned video stream, and no credentials: a viewer obtains its own scoped credentials from `POST /auth/live-credentials` and then joins these channels as a viewer. An empty array means the device is not provisioned yet, which is a 200 rather than a 404. Video frames never traverse this API.

200.description: Video channels, possibly empty if the device is not provisioned.

post.summary: Authorize the caller to subscribe to live telemetry
post.description:
The first-party dashboard's own path onto the live plane. It resolves the caller's Cognito identity from the bearer token and authorizes that identity to connect to the realtime broker and subscribe to `xorgate/devices/{deviceId}/telemetry`. Idempotent, so calling it on every page load is fine.

**Third parties do not use this.** `POST /auth/live-credentials` is the third-party entry to the live plane: it needs no Cognito identity, works with any of the three credentials, and comes back scoped to the caller's organization or workspace. This operation exists because a browser federated through the identity pool is authorized by a different mechanism, and it is org-blind in what it lets you SUBSCRIBE to.

**Use the returned `identityId` as the prefix of your client id.** Connect is scoped to `client/<identityId>*`, so a connection presenting any other client id is refused. Append something random after the identity id (xorgate-web uses `<identityId>-<role>-<uuid>`): one identity legitimately holds several concurrent connections, and two browser tabs of the same user resolve to the SAME identity id, so a bare identity id would make your own connections displace each other.

Requires membership of at least one organization, not merely a valid token. Losing your last membership therefore ends live access rather than merely un-attaching something you could immediately re-attach.

**Cognito ID token only.** The grant hangs off the caller's Cognito identity, which an API key does not have; a key is refused with `401 USER_CREDENTIAL_REQUIRED`.

identityId.description: The Cognito identity id that was authorized, and the required prefix of the client id you connect with.

delete.summary: Revoke your own access to the live plane
delete.description:
The counterpart to `POST /live/access`: withdraws the authorization from the Cognito identity behind your bearer token, after which the broker refuses that identity's next connection and any live subscription dies on its next reconnect. Idempotent — revoking access you do not have returns the same 200.

Self-service only. Revoking someone else's live access is a consequence of removing their membership: `DELETE /memberships/{id}` revokes automatically when the removal takes away their LAST organization membership. It deliberately does not fire while the user still belongs to another organization, because the grant is one shared org-blind authorization and they remain entitled to it.

Unlike the grant, this needs only a valid token and no organization membership: someone who has just lost their last membership must still be able to clean up after themselves.

**Cognito ID token only**, for the same reason as the grant: there is no Cognito identity behind an API key to revoke (`401 USER_CREDENTIAL_REQUIRED`).

200.description: The caller identity is no longer authorized.

identityId.description: The Cognito identity id the authorization was removed from.

get.summary: List workflow templates
get.description:
Every template in the active organization, newest-updated first. Paginated with the shared list dialect, and filterable by `status` and by `tag`.

`tag` is what makes this endpoint useful to a program: tag the templates your integration owns, then find them by that tag rather than by name or id. Repeating the parameter and comma-separating its values are the same request, and the semantics are ANY-of: `?tag=geofence&tag=speeding` returns templates carrying EITHER. There is no ALL-of mode.

Rows carry the metadata and the tags, not the graph. Read one template to get its versions and their definitions.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Sort column. Anything else is a 400.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Narrow to one status. Empty or `any` means no filter; anything else is a 400.

parameters.name: tag
parameters.description: Return templates carrying at least one of these tags (ANY-of). Values are normalized like stored tags, so `?tag=Geofence` matches `geofence`; a value that cannot be a tag at all is a 400. At most 20 values.

get.summary: List the organization's workflow template tags
get.description: Every distinct tag used in the active organization with the number of templates carrying it, most used first and alphabetical within a count. One query over the organization's templates, meant for populating a picker without paging the collection. An organization whose templates are all untagged gets an empty array.

200.description: The tag vocabulary of this organization

get.summary: Get a workflow template
get.description:
The template plus its full version history and the devices it is attached to. Each version carries its graph in `definition`, in the engine's definition format, upgraded to the current schema version on read.

A template belonging to another organization answers `404`, like every other org-scoped resource: you cannot tell "does not exist" from "not yours".

get.summary: List webhook endpoints
get.description: The organization's endpoint registry, paginated with the shared list dialect, newest first by default. Any role may read. A workspace-scoped session token is refused (`403 WORKSPACE_SCOPED`): endpoints are organization resources.

200.description: Endpoints. The signing secret is never included.

post.description:
Creates an endpoint and its signing secret, returned exactly once as `secret` (`whsec_` + base64 of 32 random bytes, the Standard Webhooks format). Deliveries carry `webhook-id`, `webhook-timestamp` and `webhook-signature` headers; verify them with any Standard Webhooks library.

`name` is the handle a workflow template's `output.event` node references in its `webhook` field; it is unique within the organization. `url` must be `https://`, carry no credentials, and not be `localhost` or a literal private, loopback or link-local address. Redirects are never followed.

An endpoint receives nothing until something routes to it: a device route (`PUT /devices/{id}/webhooks`) or a workflow node naming it. `POST /webhooks/{id}/test` sends a `ping`.

201.description: Created. Save `secret`: it is not retrievable later, only rotatable.

get.summary: Get a webhook endpoint
get.description: The endpoint plus `deliveryStats`: delivery counts by status over the last 24 hours.

patch.description: Any of `name`, `url`, `description`, `enabled`. Disabling records `disabledAt` and `disabledReason: "manual"`; re-enabling clears them and resets `consecutiveFailures`. An endpoint that answered `410 Gone` is disabled automatically (`disabledReason: "gone"`), and so is one with 5 exhausted deliveries in a row whose oldest exhaustion is at least 24 h old (`disabledReason: "failing"`; the org owners are emailed).

delete.description: Deletes the endpoint, its device routes, its delivery log and its signing secret. Past events stay in the organization's event history.

post.description: Emits a `ping` event to this endpoint only. One attempt, never retried; the result appears in `GET /webhooks/{id}/deliveries` within seconds. `dispatched: false` means the event was recorded but webhook delivery is switched off for this deployment.
Returns a new `secret` exactly once. For 24 hours deliveries carry TWO `v1,` signatures (new and previous), which Standard Webhooks verifiers accept, so the receiver can switch at its own pace.

get.summary: List deliveries to an endpoint
get.description: The delivery log, newest first by default, paginated with the shared list dialect. Kept for 30 days. `status`: `pending` (queued or waiting to retry), `delivered` (2xx), `failed` (a ping that failed, a 410, or a disabled endpoint), `exhausted` (8 attempts over about 44 hours, all failed).

post.description: Queues a NEW delivery of the same event (same `webhook-id`, so a receiver that dedupes on it will treat it as a repeat) with a fresh retry schedule. `redeliveryOf` points at the original.

get.summary: List webhook event types
get.description: Every event type with how it is routed and a sample `data`. `device` types are routed per device (`PUT /devices/{id}/webhooks`); `workflow.event` by the emitting node's `webhook` field; `ping` by `POST /webhooks/{id}/test`.

get.summary: Get a device's webhook routes
get.description: Which endpoints receive which of this device's presence and session events. owner/admin/member. A workspace-scoped session token may read its own workspace's devices.

put.summary: Replace a device's webhook routes (owner/admin only)
put.description: The body is the complete set; `{"routes": []}` removes every route. Each endpoint may appear once, with a non-empty subset of the device event types. Endpoints must belong to the organization. Adding a route applies to events from then on (no backfill). A workspace-scoped session token may manage its own workspace's devices, which is how an integration wires a device at pairing time.

get.summary: Cross-resource search within the active organization
get.description: A jump-to-detail navigator, not a result browser. It matches devices by name or serial (and workflow resources, which are not part of this documented surface yet), returns at most 6 hits per resource type, and normalizes every hit to `{type, id, title, subtitle}` so one code path can render them all. A `q` shorter than 2 characters returns an empty list rather than an error, and `%` or `_` are matched literally.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Search term. Substring match, case-insensitive.

get.description: Unauthenticated liveness probe. It does not touch the database, so a 200 means the Lambda is warm and reachable, not that the platform is fully healthy.
